body.text: bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s> (Treatise on the Scripture of the Arising of the Mind of Awakening)

body.text: prathamo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: First Chapter

body.text: adhyeṣaṇotpādaḥ

children.translated_text: I bow to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who have gone [to awakening], limitless in number —
the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) of the present and those yet to come;
whose minds are unshakeable like space, who are unconquered,
and who are of great compassion, [dedicated] to rescuing beings. || 1 ||

body.translated_text: The Arising of the Aspiration (<s>Adhyeṣaṇotpāda</s>)

body.text: 1 | asti mahāvaipulyamanuttaraṃ saddharmamātṛkāpiṭakaṃ bodhisatvai rmahāsattvairabhyastam | tathāhi | (1) adhyepatantyabhisamboddhu manuttarāṃ bodhim | (2) prerayanti sattvān cittamutpādayituṃ gambhīrodāram | (3) pratiṣṭhāpayanti praṇidhānaṃ pariniṣpannam | (4) utsṛjantyātmabhāvaṃ dhanāni ca nigṛhṇanti lobhaṃ mātsarya ca | (5) ācaranti pacaskandhaśīlam | vinayanti cāparādhinaḥ | (6) bhāvayanti paramāṃ kṣāntiṃ dveṣāparaṇanigrahāya (7) janayanti voryotsāhaṃ sattvapratiṣṭhāpanāya (8) saṃgṛhṇanti dhyānāni sattvacittaparijñānāya | (9) bhāvayanti prajñāmavidyānirodhāya | (10) praviśanti tathatādvāramāsaṅgaprahāṇāya | (11) pradarśayānti gaṃbhīratamāmalakṣaṇāṃ śūnyatācaryām | (12) anuśaṃsanti puṇyaṃ buddhabījānucchedāya | ityevamādīnaprameyānupāyān bodhidharmasahāyabhūtāni viśuddhimukhāni sarvebhyo 'nuttarakuśalakāmebhyo vibhajya darśayāmi sambodhayitumanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 1. There exists the great, extensive, unsurpassed <s>saddharma-mātṛkā-piṭaka</s> (basket of the matrix of the true teaching), practiced by <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> (great bodhisattva-beings). For thus: (1) they aspire to fully awaken to the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening); (2) they impel beings to generate the profound and noble mind (<s>citta</s>); (3) they establish the perfected vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>); (4) they relinquish their own bodies and wealth, and restrain greed and jealousy; (5) they practice the fivefold discipline of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and tame offenders; (6) they cultivate supreme patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) for the restraint of hatred and harm; (7) they generate heroic vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) for the establishment of beings; (8) they gather the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) for the thorough knowledge of the minds of beings; (9) they cultivate <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) for the cessation of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>); (10) they enter the gateway of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) for the abandonment of attachment; (11) they display the practice of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), whose characteristics are most profound and stainless; (12) they extol merit for the non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s>-seed. Thus, these and other immeasurable skillful means — gateways of purification that are companions to the <s>Dharma</s> of awakening — I explain and display, distributing them to all who desire the unsurpassed wholesome, in order to awaken to the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: 2 | buddhaputrā buddhamāṣitamudgṛhṇādbhiḥ sattvānāmarthāya dharma deśyadbhi rbuddhaputraiḥ prathamaṃ tāvadanuśaṃsayitavyā buddhaguṇā yāñcchrutvā sattvāścittamutpādayeyurgaveṣayituṃ buddhaprajñām | cittotpādahetorbuddhabījamanucchinnaṃ bhavati | yadi bhikṣubhikṣuṇyuyāsakopāsikā anusmaranti buddhamanusmaranti dharmaṃ punaranusmaranti yat tathāgatā bodhisattvamārgasamprasthānakāle dharma gaveṣayitumasaṃkhyeyakalpaṃ prayatnaduḥkhamudvahantītyevamanusmṛtyā bodhisattvā nāmarthāya deśayanti dharma yāvadekāmapi gāthāṃ yena dharmamimaṃ śrutvā bodhisattvā hitāṃ deśanāmabhinandattyavaropayanti kuśalamūlānyācaranti buddhadharma prāpruvantyanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 2. The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> — the <s>Buddhaputras</s> (children of the Buddha) — who receive the teachings spoken by the <s>Buddha</s> and teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of beings, should first of all extol the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>. Having heard these, beings would generate the mind to seek the wisdom of the <s>Buddha</s>. Through the cause of generating the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>), the <s>Buddha</s>-seed remains uninterrupted. If <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers) recollect the <s>Buddha</s> and recollect the <s>Dharma</s>, and furthermore recollect that the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, at the time of setting forth on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path, sought the <s>Dharma</s> and endured the suffering of exertion for incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) — by such recollection, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit [of beings], even a single verse. Those who hear this <s>Dharma</s> and rejoice in the beneficial teaching of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> plant roots of virtue (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), practice the <s>Buddha-dharma</s>, and attain the unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: 3 | sattvānāmaprameyāṇāmanādijātimaraṇaduḥkhocchedāya bodhisattvā mahasattvā abhilaṣantyaprameyāṇi kāyacittāni | ācaranti vīryam | gambhīramutpādayantimahāpraṇidhānaṃ | anutiṣṭhanti mahopāyam | utpādayanti mahāmaitrī mahākarūṇām | gaveṣayanti mahāprajñāmadṭaṣṭoṣṇīṣalakṣaṇām ||
body.translated_text: 3. For the sake of cutting off the suffering of birth and death since beginningless time for immeasurable beings, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> aspire to immeasurable bodies and minds. They practice vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). They generate the profound, great vow (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>). They carry out great skillful means (<s>mahopāya</s>). They generate great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). They seek the great wisdom (<s>mahāprajñā</s>) marked by the [eighteen] unshared [qualities] and the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) characteristic.

body.text: 4 | gaveṣayanta evaṃvidhānmahato buddhadharmān jñātavyaṃ yad dharmā aprameyā aparyantāḥ | dharmāṇāmaprameyatvāttatpuṇyaphalavipāko 'pyaprameyaḥ | bhagavānavocat | bodhisattvāścedādivodhicittamutpādayanti teṣāṃ tasya durbalasyāpi kṣaṇasya puṇyaphalavipākaḥ kalpakoṭiśatasahasrairapi vaktuṃ na pāryate kathaṃ puarekadinamekamāsamekavarṣa yāvacchatavarṣaṃ samprasthitasya cittasya puṇyaphalavipāko vaktuṃ pāryeta | tatkasya hetoḥ | sarvānsattvānsthāpayitumanutpādadharmakṣāntāvabhisaṃbodhayiumanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhiḥ bodhisattvacaryāyā anantatvāt ||
body.translated_text: 4. While seeking such great <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, it should be known that the <s>dharmas</s> are immeasurable and boundless. Because the <s>dharmas</s> are immeasurable, the fruit and ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) of the merit [associated with them] is also immeasurable. The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said: 'If <s>Bodhisattvas</s> generate the initial mind of awakening (<s>ādibodhicitta</s>), the fruit and ripening of the merit of even that weak moment cannot be expressed in hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>kalpas</s>. How then could the fruit and ripening of the merit of one who has set forth for one day, one month, one year, or even a hundred years be expressed? For what reason? Because the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice is infinite, [aimed at] establishing all beings in the patience of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpādadharma-kṣānti</s>) and fully awakening them to the unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: 5 | buddhatmajā bodhisattvā ādibodhicittamutpādayanti | tathāhi | mahāsamudro yadādau samudeti jñātavyaḥ so 'dhamamadhyamottamamūlyānāṃ yāvadmulyānāṃ cintāmaṇiratnamuktāphalānāmākaro bhavati | eṣāṃ ratnānāṃ mahāsamudrādutpatteḥ | bodhisattvasya cittotpādā apyevam | yadādicittamutpadyate jñātavyaṃ taddevamanuṣyāṇāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ sarvakuśaladharmāṇāṃ dhyānasya prajñāyāścotpatterākaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: 5. The sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, generate the initial mind of awakening (<s>ādibodhicitta</s>). For thus: just as when the great ocean first arises, it should be known that it becomes the mine of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling) gems, pearls, and other treasures of inferior, middling, and superior value — because these jewels arise from the great ocean. In the same way, when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s initial mind arises, it should be known that it becomes the mine for the arising of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) for gods and humans, <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas), and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: 6 | punastathāhi | trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturyadā samudeti jñātavyaṃ tatra ye paṃcaviṃśatirbhavā steṣu yāvantaḥ sattvāḥ sarvānvahati sarveṣāmāśrayo bhavatyāvāso bhavati | bodhisattvasya cittotpādā apyevam | yadā tatsamudeti sarveṣāmāśrayo bhavatyaprameyāṇāṃ sattvānām | ṣaḍgatiṣu caturyoniṣu ye samyagmithyādṭaṣṭayo 'bhyastakuśalābhyastākuśalā rakṣitaśuddhaśīlakṛtacaturgurupārājikāḥ satkṛtaratnatrayaninditasaddharmāḥ samalāstairthikāḥ śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyabrāhmaṇavaiśyaśūdrāstān sarvān vahati sarveṣāmāśrayo bhavatyāvāso bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 6. Furthermore, it is thus: when the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>) comes into being, it should be known that it bears all the beings in the twenty-five states of existence (<s>bhava</s>) therein, becoming the support and dwelling-place of them all. The generation of mind by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is likewise: when it arises, it becomes the support of all immeasurable sentient beings — those in the six destinies (<s>ṣaḍgati</s>) and four modes of birth (<s>caturyoni</s>), those with right views and wrong views, those who have practiced the wholesome and those who have practiced the unwholesome, those who have guarded pure moral conduct and those who have committed the four grave defeats (<s>pārājika</s>), those who have honored the Three Jewels (<s>ratnatraya</s>) and those who have disparaged the true <s>Dharma</s>, those who are impure, <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist practitioners), <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s> — it bears them all, becoming the support and dwelling-place of them all.

body.text: 7 | punarboddhisattvo maitrī karuṇāṃ ca puraskṛtya cittamutpādayāti | maitrī bodhisattvasyāparyantāprameyā tasmādaparyantaścittotpādaḥ sattvadhātusamaḥ | tathāhi | ākāśena na kiñcidyadanāvṛtam | bodhisattvasya cittotpādā apyevamaprameyā aparyantā akṣayāḥ | ākāśasvākṣayatvātsattvā akṣayāḥ sattvānāmakṣayatvād bodhisattvasya cittotpādā api sattvadhātusamāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 7. Furthermore, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates the mind having placed <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) foremost. The <s>maitrī</s> of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> is unlimited and immeasurable; therefore the generation of mind is unlimited, equal to the realm of sentient beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>). Thus: there is nothing that space does not pervade. The generations of mind by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> are likewise immeasurable, unlimited, and inexhaustible. Since space is inexhaustible, sentient beings are inexhaustible; since sentient beings are inexhaustible, the generations of mind by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> too are equal to the realm of sentient beings.

body.text: 8 | sattvadhātornāsti paryanta iti buddhaśāsana manusṛtya saṃkṣepata ucyate | pūrvadikparyantaṃ santi koṭisahasragaṃgānadīvālukāsamā asaṃkhyeyā buddhalokadhātavaḥ | evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimottarāsu dikṣu caturṣu vidikṣūrdhvamadha ekaikasyāṃ santi koṭisahasra gaṃgānadīvālukāsamā asaṃkhyeyā buddhalokadhātavaḥ | akhilāste cūrṇitā rajāṃsi bhaveyu rnemāni rajāṃsi māṃsacakṣurgocarāṇi syuḥ | koṭiśatasahasra gaṃgānadīvālukāsameṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuṣuyāvantaḥ sattvāḥ sarvete saṃgatā udgṛhṇīyurekaṃ rajaḥ | dviguṇitakoṭiśatasahasra gaṃgānadivālukāsameṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuṣu yāvantaḥ sattvā gṛhṇīyuste dve rajasī | evaṃ viparivartanamānā udgṛhṇanto daśadikṣvekaikasyāṃ koṭisahasra gaṃgānadī bālukāsameṣva saṃkhyeyeṣu buddhalokadhātuṣu yāvatpṛthivībhṛtarajāṃsi paryantaṃ nayeyustathāpi na paryantaḥ sattavadhātoḥ | tathāhi | kaścitpuruṣaḥ keśamikaṃ śatadhā vibhajyaikena bhāgena mahāsamudjalājjalalavaṃ gṛhṇāti | mayā sattvānāṃ viṣaye bhāṣitaṃ tadevamalpaṃ yaścāpi na mayā bhāṣitaṃ tadyathā mahāsamudrajalam | yadi nāma buddho 'prameyamaparyantamasaṃkhyeyaṃ kalpamavadānaṃ vyākaroti tathāpi na paryantaḥ | bodhisattvasya cittotpādā avṛṇvantyevaṃbhūtānapi sattvān| tatkathaṃ buddhaputrāḥ | syādbodhicittasya paryantaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 8. Following the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> that the realm of sentient beings has no limit, it is said in brief: In the eastern direction, there are innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers. Likewise in the southern, western, and northern directions, in the four intermediate directions, above and below — in each there are innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers. If all of these were ground to dust, those particles would not even be within the range of the physical eye. In the innumerable great trichiliocosms equal to the sands of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, however many beings there are, if all of them assembled were to pick up one particle; in the innumerable great trichiliocosms equal to double the sands of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, however many beings there are, they would pick up two particles — continuing thus in rotation, picking up [particles] in each of the ten directions in the innumerable <s>Buddha</s>-fields equal to the sands of a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, even if they were to exhaust all the particles of earth, still the realm of sentient beings would have no limit. Thus: suppose a person were to divide the tip of a hair into a hundred parts and with one part were to take a drop of water from the great ocean. What I have spoken concerning sentient beings is that little, and what I have not spoken is like the water of the great ocean. Even if the <s>Buddha</s> were to narrate legends (<s>avadāna</s>) for immeasurable, unlimited, innumerable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), still there would be no limit. The generations of mind by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> encompass even beings of such [immeasurable number]. How then, O sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, could there be a limit to <s>bodhicitta</s>?

body.text: 9 | yadi bodhisattvā evaṃvidhaṃ bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā nottrasiṣyanti na saṃtrasiṣyanti na saṃtrāsamāpatsyante na vinivartipyante na bilayaṃ gamiṣyanti jñātavyaṃ te dhruvamutpādayiṣyanti bodhicittamiti | yadi hi sarve 'premayā buddhā aprameyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ kalpaṃ yāvadanuśaṃsanti tadguṇān tathāpi na paryantaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ | bodhicittasyāparimitatvānna paryantaḥ | ityevamādīnaprameyāṃllābhān vyākuryādyena sattvāḥ sssṛṇvantyācarantūtpāda yanti bodhicittam ||
body.translated_text: 9. If <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having heard such a teaching, will not be terrified, will not be frightened, will not fall into terror, will not turn back, and will not be dismayed — it should be known that they will certainly generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. For if all the immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s> were to praise its virtues for immeasurable and innumerable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), still there would be no limit. For what reason? Because <s>bodhicitta</s> is limitless, there is no end to it. Thus one should proclaim these and other immeasurable benefits, so that sentient beings, hearing them, may practice and generate <s>bodhicitta</s>.

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre 'vyeṣaṇotpādonāma prathamo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus ends the first chapter, named 'The Generation through Seeking,' in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>.)

body.text: dvitīyo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Second Chapter

body.text: bodhicittotpādaḥ
body.translated_text: The Generation of <s>Bodhicitta</s> (the Mind of Awakening)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathaṃ bodhicittamutpādayati | kaiśca pratyayaiḥ bodhi samudāgacchati | yadi bodhisattvaḥ paricinoti kalyāṇamitrāṇi | pūjayati buddhān saṃgṛhṇāti kuśalamūlāni | gavepayati praṇītadharmān | bhavati nityaṃ suratacittaḥ | kṣamate duḥkhānyāpatitāni | bhavati maitraḥ kāruṇika ṛjucittaḥ | bhavati samacittaśayaḥ | śraddhayābhinandati mahāyānam | gaveṣayati buddhaprajñām | yadi puruṣasya santime daśadharmā utpādayatyanuttarasamyaksamboddicittam ||
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> generate <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening)? And by what conditions does <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) come to be fully realized? If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivates virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), worships the <s>Buddhas</s>, gathers roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), seeks the sublime <s>Dharma</s>, is always of a loving mind, endures sufferings that have befallen [him], is friendly, compassionate, and straightforward in mind, is of equal mental disposition, embraces the <s>Mahāyāna</s> with faith, and seeks the wisdom of the <s>Buddha</s> — if a person possesses these ten qualities, he generates the mind of supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksambodhi</s>).

body.text: 2 | punaścatvāraḥpratyayā yaiścittamutpādayati saṃgrahītumanuttarāṃ bodhim | katame catbāraḥ | anuvicintayanbuddhānbodhicittamutpādayatīti prathamaḥ | pratyavekṣamāṇakāyasyādīnavān bodhicittamutpādayatīti dvitīyaḥ | dayamānaḥ sattveṣu bodhicittamutpādayatīti tṛtīyaḥ | gaveṣayannuttamaṃ phalaṃ bodhicittamutpādayatīi caturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 2. Furthermore, there are four conditions by which one generates the mind to attain supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). What are the four? Contemplating the <s>Buddhas</s>, one generates <s>bodhicitta</s> — this is the first. Reflecting on the defects of the body, one generates <s>bodhicitta</s> — this is the second. Having compassion toward sentient beings, one generates <s>bodhicitta</s> — this is the third. Seeking the supreme fruit, one generates <s>bodhicitta</s> — this is the fourth.

body.text: 3 | buddhānuvicintanā punaḥ pañcaprakārā | anuvicintayati yaddaśadikṣvatītānāgatapratyutpannāḥ sarve buddhāścittotpādārambhe 'dhunāhamivāsan kleśasvabhāvāante cābhavansamyaksambuddhā anuttarā bhagavanta iti heto rbodhicittamutpādayāmīti prathamā | anuvicintayati yat sarve triṣvadhvasu buddhā mahotsāhamudapādayan pṛthakpṛthagvāptumanuttarāṃ bodhim | yadi bodhiḥ prāptavyo dharmo mayāpi prāptavyetihetorutpādayāmi bodhicittamiti dvitīyā | anuvicintayati yatsarve triṣvadhvasu buddhā udapādayanmahāprajñāṃ pratyatiṣṭhipannādyāvaraṇe varacittaṃ saṃcinvanto duṣkaracaryāmudadīdharannātmānamatyakramiṣustridhātum | ahamapyevamātmānamuddhareyamiti hetorutpādayāmi bodhicittamiti tṛtītā | anuvicintayati yatsarve triṣvadhvanu buddhā lokanāyakāḥ pāraṃgatā jātijarāmaraṇakleśamahāsamudāt | ahamapi puruṣaḥ pāraṃ brajeyamiti hetoratpādayāmi bodhicittamiti caturthī | anuvicintayati yatsarve tripvadhvasu buddhā udapādayanmahāvīryamudasṛjannātmabhāvaṃ jīvitaṃ dhanāni cāmārgayansarvajñatām | ahamapi sāmpratamanusareyaṃ buddhāniti hetorutpādayāmi bodhicittamiti paṃcamī ||
body.translated_text: 3. The contemplation of the <s>Buddhas</s> is again of five kinds: One contemplates that all <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present in the ten directions, at the beginning of generating the mind, were like me now, of the nature of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and in the end became supreme, perfectly awakened <s>Bhagavāns</s> (Blessed Lords) — therefore I shall generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. This is the first. One contemplates that all <s>Buddhas</s> in the three times generated great vigor, each striving individually to attain supreme <s>bodhi</s>; if awakening is a <s>dharma</s> to be attained, then I too should attain it — therefore I generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. This is the second. One contemplates that all <s>Buddhas</s> in the three times generated great wisdom (<s>mahāprajñā</s>), stood firm against the foremost obstacles, accumulated merit with excellent minds, undertook difficult practices, and transcended the three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>); I too should thus lift myself up — therefore I generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. This is the third. One contemplates that all <s>Buddhas</s> in the three times, leaders of the world, went beyond the great ocean of birth, old age, death, and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); I too, being a person, should go beyond — therefore I generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. This is the fourth. One contemplates that all <s>Buddhas</s> in the three times generated great heroic energy (<s>mahāvīrya</s>), relinquished their own bodies, lives, and wealth, seeking omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>); I too should now follow the <s>Buddhas</s> — therefore I generate <s>bodhicitta</s>. This is the fifth.

body.text: 4 | kāyasyādīnavapratyavekṣā bodhicittotpādāya punaḥ paṃcaprakārā | ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣate yatkāye 'sminnubhaye pañcaskandhāścaturmahābhūtāni kurvantyaprameyāṇyaśubhakarmāṇītikāmayate tatparityāgamiti prathamā | ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣate yatkāye 'sminnavacchidrāṇi yebhyaḥ sravanti durgandhimalāmedhyānīti kurute taṃ pratyanādaramitidvitīyā | ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣate yatkāye 'smillobhadveṣamohā aprameyāḥ kleśā nirdahanti kuśalacittamiti kāmayate nirvāpayitumiti tṛtīyā | ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣate yatkāyo 'yaṃ phenabudbudavatkṣaṇaṃkṣaṇamutpadyate nirudhyate tena dharmāḥ prahātavyā iti kāmayate prahātumiti caturthī | ātmānaṃ pratyavekṣate yatkāyo 'yamavidyāvṛtatayā sarvadā karityaśubhakarmāṇi saṃsarati ṣaḍgatiṣu na cāsya lābha iti paṃcamī |
body.translated_text: 4. The reflection on the defects of the body for generating <s>bodhicitta</s> is again of five kinds: One reflects upon oneself that in this body the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and four great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) perform immeasurable unwholesome actions — [therefore] one desires to abandon it. This is the first. One reflects upon oneself that from the nine apertures in this body flow forth foul-smelling impurities and filth — [therefore] one regards it with disregard. This is the second. One reflects upon oneself that in this body, greed, hatred, and delusion — immeasurable <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — burn up the wholesome mind; [therefore] one desires to extinguish them. This is the third. One reflects upon oneself that this body, like foam and bubbles, arises and ceases moment by moment; therefore <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are to be abandoned — one desires to abandon them. This is the fourth. One reflects upon oneself that this body, being covered by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), always performs unwholesome actions and transmigrates through the six destinies (<s>ṣaḍgati</s>), and there is no gain from it. This is the fifth.

body.text: 5 | uttamaphalagaveṣaṇā bodhicittotpādāya punaḥ paṃcaprakārā | paśyati tathāgatānāṃ bhāsvaranirmalāṃ sallakṣaṇānuvyañjananiṣpattiṃ yāṃ saṃgacchataḥ kleśā vyapagatā bhavantīti saṃgṛhṇatīti prathamā | paśyati tathāgatānāṃ dharmakāyaṃ nityamavasthitaṃ pariśuddhaṃ niṣkalaṃkamiti saṃgṛhṇatīti dvitīyā | paśyati tathāgatānāṃ śīlasamādhiprajñāvimuktivimuktijñānadarśanapariśuddhadharmaskandhāmiti saṃgṛhṇatīti tṛtīyā | paśyati tathāgatānāṃ daśa balāni catvāri vaiśaradyāni mahākaruṇāṃ trīṇi smṛtyupasthānānīti saṃgṛhṇatīti caturthī | paśyati tathāgatānāṃ sarvajñatāṃ kṛpāṃ sattveṣu yanmaitrīkaruṇābhyāṃ samāvṛtya vibhrāntānnayati sarvānsanmārgamiti saṃgṛhṇatīti pañcamī ||
body.translated_text: 5. The seeking of the supreme fruit for the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) is again fivefold: First, one sees the radiant, stainless perfection of the excellent marks and secondary characteristics of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, [and understands] that for one who encounters this, defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) become eliminated — and one grasps this. Second, one sees the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> as permanent, stable, purified, and stainless — and one grasps this. Third, one sees the pure <s>dharma</s>-aggregates of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> consisting of <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>vimukti</s> (liberation), and <s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s> (knowledge and vision of liberation) — and one grasps this. Fourth, one sees the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), and three foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — and one grasps this. Fifth, one sees the omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) and compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> toward beings — that through <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), embracing all wandering beings, they lead them to the right path — and one grasps this.

body.text: 6 | kṛpā sattveṣu bodhicittotpādāya punaḥ pañcaprakārā | paśyati sattvānavidyayā vinibaddhāniti prathamā | paśyati satvānnānāduḥkhaparyavasthitāniti dvitīyā | paśyati sattvansaṃgṛhṇato 'kuśalakarmāṇīti tṛtīyā | paśyati sattvānkurvato gurutarāṇi duścaritānīti caturthī | paśyatisattvānanācarataḥ samyagdharmamiti pañcamī ||
body.translated_text: 6. Compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) toward beings for the generation of <s>bodhicitta</s> is again fivefold: First, one sees beings bound by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Second, one sees beings beset by various sufferings. Third, one sees beings accumulating unwholesome actions (<s>akuśalakarma</s>). Fourth, one sees beings committing severe misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>). Fifth, one sees beings not practicing the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>samyagdharma</s>).

body.text: 7 | avidyābandhanaṃ punaścatuḥprakāram | paśyati sattvānmoharāgavibhrāntānvedayato mahākṛcchraduḥkhānīti prathamam | paśyati sattvānaśraddadhānānhetuphalayoḥ kurvato 'śubhakarmāṇīti dvitīyam | paśyati sattvānutsṛjataḥ samyagdharmaṃ śraddadhānān mṛṣāmārgamiti tṛtīyam | paśyati sattvānkleśanadyāṃ majjataścatuḥpravāheṣūnmajjata iti caturtham ||
body.translated_text: 7. The bondage of ignorance (<s>avidyābandha</s>) is again fourfold: First, one sees beings deluded by confusion and passion (<s>moharāga</s>), experiencing great hardship and suffering. Second, one sees beings without faith (<s>aśraddadhāna</s>) in cause and effect, performing unwholesome actions (<s>aśubhakarma</s>). Third, one sees beings who abandon the true <s>Dharma</s> and place their faith in false paths. Fourth, one sees beings drowning in the river of defilements (<s>kleśanadī</s>), unable to surface from its four currents.

body.text: 8 | nānāduḥkhaparyavasthānaṃ punaścatuḥprakāram | paśyati sattvānbibhyato jātijarāvyādhimaraṇebhyo vimokṣamagaveṣayataḥ karmāṇi punaḥ kurvata iti prathamam | paśyati sattvāñcchokaparidevadaurmanasyaduḥkhitānnityamaviśrāntakarmaṇa iti dvitīyam | paśyati sattvānpriyaviyogaduḥkhamūḍhānupāyāsaktāniti tṛtīyam | paśyati sattvānapriyasaṃyogaduḥkhitānnityamatikrāntabhederṣyānapi kṛtāpriyāniti caturtham ||
body.translated_text: 8. Being beset by various sufferings is again fourfold: First, one sees beings who, fearing birth, old age, disease, and death, yet not seeking liberation, continue to perform [unwholesome] actions. Second, one sees beings afflicted by grief, lamentation, dejection, and suffering (<s>śokaparidevaduḥkha</s>), with their actions never at rest. Third, one sees beings confused by the suffering of separation from the beloved, attached to [wrong] means. Fourth, one sees beings suffering from the conjunction with the unloved, constantly transgressing boundaries through envy, even toward those who have been made dear.

body.text: 9 | akuśalasaṃgrahaḥpunaścatuḥprakāraḥ | paśyati sattvānkāmārāgātkurvato 'śubhāniti prathamaḥ | paśyati sattvāñjānato 'pi kāmānāṃ duḥkhotpādakatamanutsṛjataḥ kāmāniti dvitīyaḥ | paśyati sattvānsukhaṃ kāmayato 'pi śīlapādavimukhāniti tṛtīyaḥ | paśyati sattvānduḥkhamanabhinandato 'pi carato 'virataṃ duḥkhāyeti caturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 9. The accumulation of the unwholesome (<s>akuśalasaṃgraha</s>) is again fourfold: First, one sees beings performing unwholesome acts out of sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>). Second, one sees beings who, even though knowing the suffering-producing nature of sensual pleasures, do not abandon them. Third, one sees beings who, though desiring happiness, turn away from the foundation of moral conduct (<s>śīlapāda</s>). Fourth, one sees beings who, though not rejoicing in suffering, ceaselessly engage in what leads to suffering.

body.text: 10 | gurutarapāpācāraḥ punaścatuḥprakāraḥ | paśyati sattvānaparādhyatoguruśīlaṃ bhaye 'pi pramādina iti prathamaḥ | paśyatisattvānkurvato 'tyantāśubhāni pañcānantaryakarmāṇi drohāvṛtatvena notpādayato hriyamapatrapāṃceti dvitīyaḥ | paśyati sattvānnindato mahāyānavaipulyasaddharmānvālyaparigṛhītānsamudgatamadamānāniti tṛtīyaḥ | paśyati sattvānbuddhimato 'pyucchindataḥ kuśalamūlānyathāpi mānino na kadāpyanuśocata iti caturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 10. Severe sinful conduct (<s>gurutarapāpācāra</s>) is again fourfold: First, one sees beings who transgress the grave [rules of] morality, who are heedless even in danger. Second, one sees beings who commit the extremely unwholesome five acts of immediate [retribution] (<s>pañcānantaryakarma</s>), who through treachery and obscuration do not generate shame (<s>hrī</s>) or moral dread (<s>apatrapā</s>). Third, one sees beings who disparage the <s>Mahāyāna Vaipulya</s> true <s>Dharma</s>, who are seized by foolishness, swollen with arrogance and pride. Fourth, one sees beings who, though intelligent, cut off their roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>), and who, though still proud, never feel remorse.

body.text: 11 | samyagdharmānācaraṇaṃ punaścatuḥprakāram | paśyati sattvānaṣṭākṣaṇeṣu na śṛṇvataḥ saddharmamajānataścarituṃ kuśalamiti prathamam | paśyati sattvānbuddhotpāde nāpitaṃ saddharmaṃ śṛṇvato 'pi na gṛhṇata iti dvitīyam | paśyati sattvānudgṛhṇata stairthikavādānkurvata ātmaklamathānuyogān nityamapagacchato vimokṣāditi tṛtīyam | dṛśyati sattvāṃllabdhaṃ naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāṃ nāma samādhi nirvāṇamivodgṛhṇataḥ kuśalavipākānte punaścyavatastisṛtiṣu durgatiṣviti caturtham ||
body.translated_text: 11. Not practicing the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>samyagdharmānācaraṇa</s>) is again fourfold: First, one sees beings in the eight unfavorable conditions (<s>aṣṭākṣaṇa</s>), not hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>, not knowing how to practice what is wholesome. Second, one sees beings who, even at the time of a <s>Buddha</s>'s arising, even when hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> that has not been lost, do not grasp it. Third, one sees beings who take up the doctrines of <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers), who practice self-mortification, constantly moving away from liberation. Fourth, one sees beings who, having attained the <s>samādhi</s> called 'neither-perception-nor-non-perception' (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñā</s>), grasp it as <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and at the end of their wholesome ripening, fall again into the three lower destinies (<s>durgati</s>).

body.text: 12 | bodhisattvaḥ paśyati sattvānavidyayākarmāṇi kurvato dīrgharātraṃ vedayato duḥkhāni parityajataḥsaddharmaṃ vismarato niḥsaraṇamārganityevaṃ kāraṇādutpādayati mahāmaitrīṃ karūṇāṃ pradīptaśirasrāṇavacca gaveṣayatyanuttarāṃ samyagyambodhiṃ sarvānsattvā keśaduḥkhitānahamuddharāmi niravaśeṣamiti | buddhātmajāḥ saṃkṣepeṇa meyadamuktam | vādikarmiko bodhisattvaḥ sakāraṇaṃ cittamutpādayatīti | vistareṇa ceducyeta na tasya parimāṇaṃ na tasya paryantaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 12. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees beings performing actions through ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), experiencing sufferings for a long time, abandoning the true <s>Dharma</s>, and forgetting the path of escape. From precisely such causes, he generates great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and as if his head were on fire, he seeks the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) [thinking]: 'I shall completely rescue all beings who suffer.' The sons of the <s>Buddha</s> — in brief, this has been stated: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is the agent of the vow generates the mind with [this] cause. Were it to be stated in detail, there would be no measure to it, no limit.

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasutraśāstre bodhicittotpādo nāma dvitīyo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the second chapter, called 'The Generation of <s>Bodhicitta</s>,' [is concluded].)

body.text: tṛtiyo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Third Chapter

body.text: pratidhānam
body.translated_text: The Vow (<s>Praṇidhāna</s>)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathamutpādayati bodhim | kayā karmacaryayā paripūrayati bodhim | utpāditacitto bodhisattvaḥ śuvidarśanābhūmi madhiṣṭhito dṭaḍhmādāvutpādayati samyakpraṇidhānaṃ saṃgrahītuṃ sarvānaprameyānsattvān | gaveṣayāmyahamanuttarāṃ bodhiṃ pāratrātuṃ niravaśepaṃ prāpayitumanupadhinirvāṇam | tasmāccittotpādādarabhya mahākaruṇāyāḥ karuṇācittenotpādayati daśottaraṇi samyakpraṇidhānāni ||
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> generate <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)? By what course of action does he fulfill <s>bodhi</s>? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated the mind, established on the ground of good vision (<s>suvidarśanābhūmi</s>), first generates the right vow (<s>samyakpraṇidhāna</s>) to embrace all immeasurable beings [thinking]: 'I seek the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> to completely rescue [all beings] and bring them to <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder (<s>anupadhinirvāṇa</s>).' Therefore, from the generation of the mind onward, with a mind of compassion born from great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), he generates the ten right vows (<s>samyakpraṇidhāna</s>).

body.text:
2 | katamāni daśa | kāmaye yanmayā purā janmanīhacānena kāyena yadavaropitaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ tadutsṛjāmyaparmantebhyaḥ sarvasattvebhyaḥ | pariṇāmayāmi ca sarvānanuttarāyāṃ bodhau | kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇaṃ praṇidhānametanme saṃvarddheta jātau jātau ca jāyeta nityaṃ cittānubaddhaṃ na kadāpi vismriyeta dhāraṇyā ca parikṣyeta |
kāmaye yadahaṃ pariṇāmya mahābodhāvanena kuśalamūlena sarvajātinivāseṣu nityaṃ pūjayeyaṃ sarvabuddhānna kadāpyabuddhakṣetreṣu saṃbhaveyam |
kāmaye yadahamutpadya buddhakṣetre ṣūpagaccheyaṃ buddhānupatiṣṭheyaṃ buddhāñchāyeva śarīramanugataḥ kṣaṇamapi na dūrībhaveyaṃ buddhebhyaḥ |
kāmaye yadahamupagato buddhāṃstai ryathākāmaṃ mamārthāya deśitena dharmeṇa niṣpādayeyaṃ bodhisattvapaṃcābhijñānāni |
kāmaye yadahaṃ niṣpādya bodhisattvapaṃcābhijñānāni saṃvṛtisatyaṃ vijñaptiprasṛtaṃ pratibudhya paramārthasatyaṃ bhṛtasvamāvaṃ parijñāya prāpnuyāṃ samyagdharmajñānam |
kāmaye yadahaṃ prāpya samyagdharmajñānamaviśrāntacittena deśayeyaṃ sattvebhyo nidarśayitumupadeśahitān ababodhayituṃ ca tānsarvān |
kāmaye yadahamababodhya sarvānsattvānbuddhānubhāvena gaccheyaṃ daśadikṣu niravaśeṣeṣu lokadhātuṣu pūjatituṃ buddhāñchrotuṃ saddarmān saṃparigrahītuṃ sattvān |
kāmaye yadahaṃ buddhakṣetreṣu saddharmamudgṛhyānupravarteyaṃ pariśuddhaṃ dharmacakram | daśadi kathātuṣu sarvesattvā mama deśanāṃ śrutvā mama nāmākarṇya parityajantu sarvānkleśānu dayantu bodhicittam |
kāmaye yadahaṃ sarvasattveṣu bodhicittamutpādya nityaṃ paripāluyituṃ parihareyamalābhaṃ prapaccheyamaprameyasukhānyutsṛjeyaṃ jīvitaṃ dhanānicoddhareyaṃ sattvānudvaheyaṃ saddharmam |
kāmaye yadahaṃ saddharmamudūḍhaya caritvāpi saddharmaṃ cittena nācareyam | yathā sattvā ācaritadharmāṇo 'pi nācaritadharmāṇo na ca nācaritadharmāṇaḥ | vinetuṃ vānnotsṛjeyaṃ samyakpraṇidhānam | itīme samutpāditacittānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ samyagmahāpraṇidhānāni | imāni daśamahāpraṇidhānāni sarvasattvadhātuṣṛdgṛhṇanti gaṃgānadībālakāsamāni praṇidhānāni | yadi ca sattvānāṃ samāptiḥ syānmama dhānānāmapi samāptirbhavet | naca khalu sattvānāṃ samāptistena mama praṇidhānānāmapi na samāptiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 2. What are the ten? [First:] 'I desire that whatever roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) I have planted in former births and in this life through this body, I relinquish to all beings without exception. And I dedicate them all to the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s>. May this vow of mine increase moment by moment, and may it arise in birth after birth, always connected to the mind, never to be forgotten, and may it be examined with <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retentive power).' [Second:] 'I desire that, having dedicated these roots of merit to the great <s>bodhi</s>, I may in all my future births always worship all <s>Buddhas</s> and never be born in <s>Buddha</s>-less realms.' [Third:] 'I desire that, born in a <s>Buddha</s>-field, I may approach the <s>Buddhas</s>, attend upon the <s>Buddhas</s>, and like a shadow following a body, never be separated from the <s>Buddhas</s> even for a moment.' [Fourth:] 'I desire that, having approached the <s>Buddhas</s>, through the <s>Dharma</s> taught by them according to my wish and for my benefit, I may accomplish the five superknowledges (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' [Fifth:] 'I desire that, having accomplished the five <s>Bodhisattva</s> superknowledges, awakening to the conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>) spread through <s>vijñapti</s> (representation), and fully understanding the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>) as one's own possession, I may attain the right knowledge of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>samyagdharmajñāna</s>).' [Sixth:] 'I desire that, having attained the right knowledge of <s>Dharma</s>, with an unwearied mind, I may teach beings, show them beneficial instruction, and awaken them all.' [Seventh:] 'I desire that, having awakened all beings, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, I may go to the world-realms in the ten directions without exception, to worship the <s>Buddhas</s>, hear the true <s>Dharma</s>, and gather beings.' [Eighth:] 'I desire that, having received the true <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Buddha</s>-fields, I may set in motion the purified wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. In all the world-realms of the ten directions, may all beings, hearing my teaching and hearing my name, abandon all defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) and generate <s>bodhicitta</s>.' [Ninth:] 'I desire that, having generated <s>bodhicitta</s> in all beings, I may always protect and guard them, ward off loss, bestow immeasurable joys, relinquish life and wealth, rescue beings, and uphold the true <s>Dharma</s>.' [Tenth:] 'I desire that, having upheld the true <s>Dharma</s>, even while practicing the true <s>Dharma</s>, I may not practice it with [attachment in] the mind. Just as beings who have practiced the <s>Dharma</s> are [paradoxically] those who have not practiced the <s>Dharma</s>, yet are not those who have not practiced the <s>Dharma</s>. Even to discipline [beings], I would not relinquish the right vow.' These are the right great vows of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have generated the mind. These ten great vows embrace all the realms of beings — vows as [numerous as] the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river. If there were an end to beings, there would be an end to my vows. But since there is no end to beings, there is no end to my vows.

body.text: 3 | punaḥ khalu dānaṃ bodhihetuḥ sarvasattvānugrāhakatvāt | śīlaṃ bodhihetuḥ daśalaprāptyā mūlapraṇihitaparipūrakatvāt | kṣāntirbodhheturdvatrīśallakṣaṇāśītyanupyañjanasaṃprāpakatvāt | vīryaṃ bodhihetuḥ kuśalācāravardhakatayā sotsāhaṃ sattvaparipācakatvāt | dhyānaṃ bodhiheturbodhisattvānāṃ samyagātmasaṃyamanena sattvacittacaryāvavodhakatvāt | prajñā bodhiheturniravaśepaṃ dharmabhāvalakṣaṇāvavodhakatvāt | saṃkṣepata ucyate ṣaḍimāḥ pāramitā bodheḥ samyaghetuḥ | catvāro brahmavihārāḥ saptaviśadbodhipākṣikā dharmā sahasraśaḥ kuśalācārāḥ sahakāriṇaḥ pūrayitāraḥ | yadi bodhisattva ācarati ṣaṭ pāramitāstadanusṛtya carati caryāṃ krameṇopaityanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 3. Furthermore, <s>dāna</s> (generosity) is a cause of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), because it benefits all beings. <s>Śīla</s> (moral conduct) is a cause of <s>bodhi</s>, because it brings about the attainment of the ten [wholesome] paths and fulfills the fundamental vow (<s>mūlapraṇidhāna</s>). <s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) is a cause of <s>bodhi</s>, because it leads to the attainment of the thirty-two major marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and eighty minor characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>). <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) is a cause of <s>bodhi</s>, because through the increase of wholesome conduct, it zealously matures beings. <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is a cause of <s>bodhi</s>, because through the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' proper self-restraint, it enables thorough knowledge of the conduct of the minds of beings. <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) is a cause of <s>bodhi</s>, because it enables thorough understanding of the characteristics of the nature of all <s>dharmas</s> without remainder. In brief, it is said: these six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are the proper cause of <s>bodhi</s>. The four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes), the thirty-seven <s>bodhipākṣika dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening), and the thousandfold wholesome practices are the auxiliary factors that fulfill [the cause]. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices the six <s>pāramitās</s> and accordingly follows the practice, he gradually approaches the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: 4 | buddhātmajā bodhi gaveṣayadbhirna pramaditavyam | pramādācaraṇena vinaśyatikuśalamūlam | bodhisattvo damayati ṣaḍindriyāṇi na pramādyati cedācarituṃ śaknoti ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ | bodhisattvaścittamutpādya pratiṣṭhāpayati sthairyaṃ saṃpratiṣṭhāpayati dṭaḍhaṃ praṇidhānam | praṇihitaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya na kadāpi pramādyati na ca bhavati kusīdo na ca dīrghasūtraḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ | praṇihitamadhiṣṭhitaḥ paṃcavastūnyudgṛhṇāti | dṭaḍhayati cittamiti prathamam | atikrāmyati kleśāniti dvitīyam | niruṇaddhi vicintya pramādacittamiti tṛtīyam | bhinatti paṃcanīvaraṇānīti caturtham | sotsāhamācarati ṣaṭ pāramitā iti paṃcamam | tathācānuśaṃsitaṃ bhagavatā tathāgatai rmahāprājñai rbhahāprājñai rbhagavadbhi vyākhyāteṣu guṇeṣu kṣāntiprajñāpuṇyavalānāmadhigameṣu praṇidhānabalamuttamamiti ||
body.translated_text: 4. O sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, those who seek <s>bodhi</s> must not be heedless. Through heedless conduct, roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) are destroyed. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who restrains the six sense faculties (<s>indriya</s>) and is not heedless is able to practice the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Having generated the mind, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> establishes steadfastness (<s>sthairya</s>) and firmly establishes the vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). Having established the vow, he is never heedless, nor lazy, nor procrastinating. For what reason? One who is sustained by the vow grasps five things: First, he makes the mind firm. Second, he overcomes the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Third, having reflected, he blocks the heedless mind. Fourth, he breaks through the five hindrances (<s>pañcanīvaraṇa</s>). Fifth, he zealously practices the six <s>pāramitās</s>. And thus it has been praised by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: among the qualities expounded by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of great wisdom — in the attainments of patience, wisdom, merit, and strength — 'the power of the vow (<s>praṇidhānabala</s>) is supreme.'

body.text: 5 | kathaṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati praṇidhānam | yadi kaścidāyāti bahubidhaṃ yācituṃ tadahaṃ dadāmi yāvannotpādayāmi kṣaṇamapi mātsaryacittam | kṣaṇamapinimeṣamapyutpādaya nnaśubhacittaṃ dānapratyayena cedgaveṣayāmi śubhavipākaṃ tadahaṃ pratārayāmi daśadikṣu bhagavato 'prameyānāparyantānasaṃkhyeyān pratputpannāṃstathāgatān anāgate 'śvanyapi na pūrayeyaṃ dhruvamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim | yadyahaṃdhārayāmi śīlaṃ yāvadutsṛjannapyātmabhāvaṃ (jīvitaṃ) pratiṣṭhāpayāmi pariśūddhaṃ cittaṃ praṇidadhāmi yanna pratinivarte nānuśocāmi | yadyamācarāmi kṣāntiṃ pareṇākrāntaḥ pratyaṃgaṃ vibhajyamāno 'pi cchidyamāno 'pyutpādayāmi nityaṃ maitrīṃ praṇidadhāmi yannācareyaṃ dveṣam | yadyahamācarāmi vīryamupalabhya śītoṣṇarājadasyujalāgnisiṃhavyāghravṛkanirjakāntārān dṭaḍhikaromi cittaṃ praṇidadhāmi yanna pratinivarte | yadyahaṃ bhāvayāmi dhyānaṃ bāhyai rvastubhiḥ kliśyamāno 'pi vyākulacittau 'pyanubadhnāmi smṛtiṃ karmasthāne | kṣaṇamapi na kadācidutpādayāmyadharmyāṃ vikṣepasaṃjñām | yadyahaṃ bhāvayāmi prajñāṃ sarvadharmāstathatābhūtānpaśyanparigṛhṇapi | kuśalākuśaleṣu saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛteṣu jātimaraṇanirvāṇeṣu notpādayāmi dvaitadṭaṣṭim | yadyahaṃ nimeṣamapi kṣaṇamapyanuśocandviṣan pratinivartamānaḥ saṃjñāṃ vikṣipan dvaitadṭaṣṭimutpādayañchilakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñābhiḥ śubhavipākaṃ gaveṣayāmi tadahaṃ pratārayāmi daśadiglokadhātuṣvaprameyānaparyantānasaṃkhyeyān pratyutpannāṃstathāgatān | anāgate 'dhvanyapi na khalupūrayeyamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim |
body.translated_text: 5. How does one establish the vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>)? 'If anyone comes to ask for many kinds of things, I shall give — and I shall not generate a jealous mind (<s>mātsaryacitta</s>) even for an instant. If, even for an instant or the blink of an eye, generating an unwholesome mind, I should seek a favorable ripening through the condition of giving, then I would deceive the immeasurable, boundless, incalculable <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the present in the ten directions, and in the future too I would surely never fulfill the unsurpassed perfect awakening.' 'If I maintain <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) — even relinquishing my own body and life — I shall establish a purified mind and make the vow that I shall not turn back and shall not grieve.' 'If I practice <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), even when assaulted by others, even when being dismembered limb by limb, even when being cut — I shall always generate <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and make the vow that I shall not practice hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>).' 'If I practice <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), encountering cold, heat, kings, bandits, floods, fire, lions, tigers, wolves, and waterless wilderness — I shall make my mind firm and make the vow that I shall not turn back.' 'If I cultivate <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), even when afflicted by external objects, even when my mind is disturbed — I shall bind my mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) to the meditation object. Even for an instant I shall never generate the notion of unwholesome distraction.' 'If I cultivate <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), I shall embrace them. With regard to wholesome and unwholesome, conditioned and unconditioned, birth-and-death and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — I shall not generate a dualistic view.' 'If I, even for the blink of an eye or a moment, grieving, hating, turning back, generating distracted notions, or generating a dualistic view, should seek a favorable ripening through <s>śīla</s>, <s>kṣānti</s>, <s>vīrya</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, and <s>prajñā</s>, then I would deceive the immeasurable, boundless, incalculable <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the present in the world-realms of the ten directions. And in the future too, I would surely never fulfill the unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: 6 | bodhisattvo daśamahāpraṇidhānai rgṛhṇāti saddharmacaryām | ṣaṇmahā praṇidhānai rdamayati prāmadacittam | sotsāhaṃ varati vīryam | ācarati ṣat pāramitāḥ paripūrayatyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim ||
body.translated_text: 6. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> undertakes the practice of the true <s>Dharma</s> through ten great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>). Through six great vows he tames the heedless mind. With vigor he energetically exerts himself. He practices the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) and fulfills the supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasutraśātre praṇidhānaṃ nāma tṛtīyo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the third chapter named 'The Vow' (<s>praṇidhāna</s>).)

body.text: caturtho vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Fourth Chapter

body.text: dānapāramitā
body.translated_text: <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Giving)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathaṃ dānaṃ dadāti | dānamātmaparobhayalābhāya cedevaṃvidhaṃ dānaṃ niṣpādayati bodhimārgam | bodhisattvaḥ kāmayate vinetuṃ sattvānaparhatuṃ duḥkhāni dadāti tasmāddānam | dānamutsṛjannityamutpādayatyātmavitteṣu tyāgacittam | yācakeṣu mātāpitṛgurukalyāṇamitreṣvivotpādayatyādaracittam | janayati mātāpitṛgurukalyāṇamitrasaṃjñām | putra ivotpādayati daridreṣu hīneṣu karuṇācittam | janayati putrasaṃjñām | yathāprārthitaṃ vitaratyādareṇa muditacittenetyucyate bodhisattvasyādidānacittam ||
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> give gifts (<s>dāna</s>)? If giving is for the benefit of oneself, others, and both, then such giving accomplishes the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, desiring to discipline beings and to remove their sufferings, therefore gives gifts. In relinquishing gifts, one always generates the mind of renunciation (<s>tyāgacitta</s>) toward one's own possessions. Toward supplicants, one generates a mind of respect as toward one's own mother, father, teacher, and virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), generating the perception of them as mother, father, teacher, and virtuous friend. Toward the destitute and lowly, one generates a mind of compassion (<s>karuṇācitta</s>) as toward one's own child, generating the perception of them as one's child. Distributing what is sought with respect and a joyful mind — this is called the initial mind of giving of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: 2 | dānacaryāhetoḥ prasarati yaśaḥ | yatra va kacijjāyate bhavantyasya prabhṛtāni dhanānītyasyātmalābhaḥ | tarpayansattvānāṃ cittaṃ śikṣayati vinayati vidadhāti tānavimatsarānityeṣa paralābhaḥ | vitarannalakṣaṇaṃ mahādānaṃ sattveṣu pariṇāmyātmanā salābhinaḥ karotītyeṣa ubhayalābhaḥ | dānacaryāhetoḥ prāpnoti vartipadam | upasaṃgṛhṇātyaprameyānsarvasattvānyāvadāprāpte rbuddhatvasyākṣayadharmakośabhyetyevaṃ niṣpādayati bodhimārgam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Through the practice of giving, one's renown spreads. Wherever one is born, one possesses abundant wealth — this is one's own benefit (<s>ātmalābha</s>). Satisfying the minds of beings, training, disciplining, and making them free from jealousy — this is the benefit of others (<s>paralābha</s>). Distributing the great gift whose characteristics are immeasurable and dedicating it to beings, thereby making them partakers of the benefit along with oneself — this is the benefit of both (<s>ubhayalābha</s>). Through the practice of giving, one attains the stage of Buddhahood (<s>vartipadam</s>). One gathers immeasurable beings until, upon attaining <s>Buddhahood</s>, one enters the inexhaustible treasury of <s>Dharma</s> — thus one accomplishes the path of awakening.

body.text: 3 | dānaṃ trividham | prathamaṃ dharmadānaṃ dvitīyamabhayadānaṃ tṛtīyamāmipadānam | dharmadānamudbodhayati lokāñchīlagrahaṇāya pravrajyācittacaraṇāya | mithyādṭaṣṭeḥ prahāṇāya deśayati śāśvatocchedau, caturaḥ viparyāsān pāpānāmādīnavaṃ ca, vibhajya prakāśayati paramārtham anuśaṃsati vīryaguṇānbhāṣate pramādātyayapāpamityucyate dharmadānam | yadi sattvo vibheti nṛpātsaṃhādvyābrādvṛkājjalādagne rdasyoścaurādvā bodhisattvo dṛṣṭe tatparitrāyat ityamayadānam | ātmano vittāni yāvad ratnaṃ hastinamaśvaṃ rathaṃ vasrāṇi dhānyaṃ vāsasī peyaṃ khādyaṃ yāvatkavalamātramekasūtraṃ prabhūtamalpaṃ vā vitaranna mātsaryaṃ kurute | yathāprārthitaṃ tarpayati yācakānityāmiṣadānam ||
body.translated_text: 3. Giving is of three kinds: first, the gift of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadāna</s>); second, the gift of fearlessness (<s>abhayadāna</s>); third, the gift of material things (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>). The gift of <s>Dharma</s> awakens worldly people to undertake moral discipline (<s>śīla</s>), to renunciation, and to the practice of mind. For the abandonment of wrong views, one teaches [the errors of] eternalism (<s>śāśvata</s>) and annihilationism (<s>uccheda</s>), the four distortions (<s>viparyāsa</s>), and the dangers of evil actions; distinguishing and illuminating the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>), extolling the virtues of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), and declaring the evil transgression of heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) — this is called the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. If a being is frightened of a king, a lion, a serpent, a wolf, water, fire, a bandit, or a thief, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, when it is seen, rescues that [being] — this is the gift of fearlessness (<s>abhayadāna</s>). One's own possessions — including gems, elephants, horses, chariots, garments, grain, clothing, drink, and food, down to a single morsel or a single thread, whether much or little — one distributes without miserliness. Satisfying supplicants according to their wishes — this is the gift of material things (<s>āmiṣadāna</s>).

body.text: 4 | āmiṣadānaṃ punaḥ pañcavidham | prathamaṃ saralacittadānaṃ dvitīyaṃ śraddhā cittadānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ yathākāladānaṃ caturthaṃ svahastena dānaṃ paṃcamaṃ yathādharmadānam ||
body.translated_text: 4. The gift of material things is again fivefold: first, giving with a sincere mind; second, giving with a faithful mind; third, giving at the appropriate time; fourth, giving with one's own hand; fifth, giving in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: 5 | adātavyaṃ dānaṃ punaḥ paṃcaprakāram | adharmeṇopārjitaṃ dhanaṃ na dātavyaṃ syāpariśūddhatvāt | madyaṃ na dātavyaṃ parebhyo viṣaṃ ca sattvānāṃ vikṣepasattvāt | mṛgayopakaraṇāni na dātavyāni parebhyassattvānāṃ kleśakaratvāt | na dātavyāḥ parebhyassattvānāṃ hisakatvāt | gītaṃ striyaśca na dātavyāḥ parebhyaścittapavitratāyā dūṣakatvāt | saṃkṣepata ucyate | yanna yathādharmaṃ yacca vikṣepakaraṃ vikṣepakaraṃ sattvānāṃ tanna dātavyaṃ parebhyaḥ | śiṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ yatsukhayati sattvāṃstaducyate yathādharmadānam ||dānaricirlabhate paṃcabidhaṃ kīrtikuśalalābham | sāmīpyaṃ labhate sarvasatāmiti prathamaḥ | sarve sattvāstaṃ draṣṭumabhilaṣantīti dvitīyaḥ | janakāyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ satkriyate janairiti tṛtīyaḥ | prasarannasya yaśovarṇaḥ śrūyate daśasu dikṣviti caturthaḥ | bhavati bodheḥ samyaguttamo heturiti paṃcamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 5. There are again five kinds of gifts that should not be given: Wealth acquired by unrighteous means should not be given, because it is impure. Intoxicants and poison should not be given to others, because they cause distraction and harm to beings. Hunting implements should not be given to others, because they cause affliction (<s>kleśa</s>) to beings. Weapons should not be given to others, because they cause injury to beings. Songs and women should not be given to others, because they corrupt the purity of mind. Stated briefly: whatever is not in accordance with <s>Dharma</s> and whatever causes distraction and harm to beings should not be given to others. Everything else that brings happiness to beings is called giving in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>. The practitioner of giving obtains fivefold renown and wholesome benefit: one gains the proximity of all good people — this is the first. All beings wish to see that person — this is the second. Having entered an assembly, one is honored by the people — this is the third. One's renown and good repute spread and are heard in the ten directions — this is the fourth. It becomes the supreme and right cause of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) — this is the fifth.

body.text: 6 | bodhisattvaḥ sarvadātetyucyate | sarvadānaṃ na bahudhanaṃ kintu dānacittam | yathādharmaṃ dhanamupārjyopādāya yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam pariśuddhacittena yadaśāṭhayadānaṃ taducyate sarvadānam | daridrāndṭaṣṭrā dayācittena yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | duḥkhitāndṭaṣṭrā karuṇācittena yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | daridro 'lpadhano 'pi yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | spṛhaṇīyāni ratnajātānyudāracittena yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | apaśyañchīlāśīlaṃ kṣetrākṣetraṃ yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam apaśyaz ṇchilāśīlaṃ kṣetākṣetraṃ yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | agaveṣayandevamānupakalyāṇasukhāni yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | gaveṣayannanuttarāṃ bodhi yaddadāti taducyate sarvadānam | ditsayā dānakāle pradāya yannānuśocati taducyate sarvadānam ||
body.translated_text: 6. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to give everything (<s>sarvadāna</s>). Giving everything is not [about] great wealth, but rather the mind of giving (<s>dānacittam</s>). Whatever one gives, having earned and acquired wealth according to <s>Dharma</s> — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives with a purified mind, without deceit — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives with a compassionate mind upon seeing the poor — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives with a mind of compassion upon seeing the suffering — that is called giving everything. Even what a poor person of little wealth gives — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives with a noble mind, [even] desirable gems and treasures — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives without regard for moral or immoral [recipients], [whether the] field or non-field — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives without seeking divine or human pleasures and well-being — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives while seeking the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> — that is called giving everything. Whatever one gives at the time of giving with a willing mind and does not regret — that is called giving everything.

body.text:
7 | yadi puṣpāṇi dadāti labhate dhāraṇīsaptabodhipuṣpāṇi | yadi gandhaṃ dadāti labhate śīlasamādhiprajñāḥ | (śīlasamādhiprajñādhūpaṃ prajvālya) dhūpayati cātmānam | yadi phalaṃ dadāti labhate pūrayati cānāsravaphalam | yadyāhāraṃ dadātikāyavāgrū pavalasukhasampannobhavati | yadi vastrāṇi dadāti labhate 'vadātaṃ rūpamapanayatyāhrīkyamanapatrāpyam | yadi pradīpaṃ dadāti buddhacakṣurlabhate bhāsvaraṃ sarvadharmasvabhāvānām | yadi hastyaśvarathayānāni dadāti labhate 'nuttaraṃ yānamṛddhiṃca | yadyalaṅkārāndadāti labhate 'śītyanuvyañjanāni | yadi ratnāni dadāti labhate dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni | pariśrameṇa [sattva-]sevāṃ yadyācarati labhate daśavalāni caturvaiśaradyāni |
saṃkṣepata ucyate | rāṣṭraṃ nagaraṃ dārānputrāñchira ścakṣura hastapādau yāvatsarvakāyaṃ dadātyantarā citramātsaryaṃ prāptamanuttarāṃ bodhiṃ parinirvāpayituṃ sattvān | bodhisattvo mahāsattva ācarandānacaryāṃ bhavatyavittadṭaṣṭi rdānādānayoralakṣaṇatvāttatasmātpūrayati dānapāramitām ||
body.translated_text: 7. If one gives flowers, one obtains the flowers of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retentive power) and the seven factors of awakening (<s>saptabodhyaṅga</s>). If one gives fragrance, one obtains <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — and having kindled the incense of morality, concentration, and wisdom, one perfumes oneself. If one gives fruit, one obtains and fulfills the fruit free from outflows (<s>anāsravaphala</s>). If one gives food, one becomes endowed with the happiness of bodily and verbal power. If one gives clothing, one obtains a pure form and removes shamelessness and lack of moral dread. If one gives a lamp, one obtains the luminous <s>Buddha</s>-eye of the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. If one gives elephants, horses, chariots, and vehicles, one obtains the unsurpassed vehicle and supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>). If one gives ornaments, one obtains the eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>). If one gives jewels, one obtains the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>). If one practices service [to beings] with effort, one obtains the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) and four fearlessnesses (<s>caturvaiśāradya</s>). Stated briefly: one gives one's kingdom, city, wife, sons, head, eyes, hands, feet, and even one's entire body — casting aside variegated avarice — in order to attain the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> and lead beings to <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, practicing the conduct of giving, becomes one who has no view of possessions — because both giving and receiving are without [fixed] characteristics — and therefore fulfills the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasṛtraśāstre dānapāramitā nāma caturtho vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the fourth chapter, called 'The Perfection of Giving (<s>Dānapāramitā</s>),' [is concluded].)

body.text: paṃcamo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Fifth Chapter

body.text: śīlapāramitā
body.translated_text: The Perfection of Morality (<s>Śīlapāramitā</s>)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathamācaratiśīlam | śīlamātmaparobhayalābhāya cedevaṃvidhaṃ śilaṃ niṣpādayati bodhimārgam | bodhisattvaḥ kāmayatevinetuṃ sattvānaparhatuṃ duḥkhānyācarati tasmācchīlam | śīlamācaransarvāṇi pavitrayati kāyavāṅmanaḥkarmāṇi | akuśalacaryāsu pariharati cittam | samyakprabhavati cāvajñāpayituṃ duṣkṛtaṃ śīlavidhātaṃ ca | kṣudreṣvapi pātakeṣu cittena vibheti nityamityucyate bodhisattvasyādiśīlacittam |
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice morality (<s>śīla</s>)? If morality is for the benefit of self, others, and both, one practices such morality [as] the path of awakening. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, desiring to discipline beings and remove sufferings, practices morality for that reason. Practicing morality, one purifies all actions of body, speech, and mind. One turns the mind away from unwholesome conduct. One rightly gives rise to [the ability] to confess wrongdoing and to establish the rules of morality. Even with regard to minor transgressions, one always fears them in one's mind — this is called the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s initial moral mind.

body.text: 2 | śīlācaraṇahetoḥ sarvān parityajati pāpātyayān kuśalāvāsepūtpadyate nityamityasyātmalābhaḥ | śikṣayati sattvānakartuṃ duṣkṛtamiti paralābhaḥ | caritvābodhaye śīlaṃ pariṇāmya sattveṣvātmanā salābhinaḥ karotityubhavalābhaḥ | śīlācaraṇahetorlabhate vairāgyaṃ yāvatkṣapayatyāsravānparipūrayati cānuttarāṃ samyaksambodhimiti niṣyādayati bodhimārgam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Through the practice of morality, one abandons all sinful transgressions and always arises in the abode of the wholesome — this is one's own benefit (<s>ātmalābha</s>). One trains beings not to commit wrongdoing — this is the benefit of others (<s>paralābha</s>). Having practiced morality for awakening, dedicating it to beings, one makes oneself and others beneficiaries — this is the benefit of both (<s>ubhayalābha</s>). Through the practice of morality, one attains dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), until one exhausts the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) and fulfills the unsurpassed perfect awakening — thus one accomplishes the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>).

body.text: 3 | śīlaṃ tāvattrividham | prathamaṃ kāyaśīlaṃ dvitīyam vākśīlaṃ tṛtīyaṃ cittaśīlam | udgṛhṇankāyaśīlaṃ sākalyena pariharatihiṃsāstainyakāmamithyācārān | virataḥ prāṇātipātādvirato 'dattādānādvirato 'brahmacaryānnapunarvidadhāti prāṇātipātādīnāṃ hetupratyāyāṃnsteṣāmupāyāṃśca na ca praharato sattvāndaṇḍena kāṣṭheneṣṭikayā prastareṇa vā | parakīyamarthajātaṃ parakīyaṃ bhogyajātaṃ yāvattṛṇamātramapi patramātramapi nādattamādatte na ca khalu punaḥ kadācidapimohakaṃ rūpaṃ nirikṣate | caturṣu sādarībhavatīryāpatheṣvityucyate kāyaśīlam ||
body.translated_text: 3. Morality (<s>śīla</s>) is indeed threefold: first, bodily morality (<s>kāyaśīla</s>); second, verbal morality (<s>vākśīla</s>); third, mental morality (<s>cittaśīla</s>). Taking up bodily morality, one completely abandons violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), theft (<s>stainya</s>), and sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>). One refrains from taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), refrains from taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>), refrains from unchastity (<s>abrahmacarya</s>), and moreover does not create the causes, conditions, or means for taking life and the rest. One does not strike beings with a stick, a piece of wood, a brick, or a stone. One does not take even as little as a blade of grass or a leaf of others' possessions or others' enjoyments that has not been given. And one never gazes upon a deluding form. One is attentive in the four modes of deportment (<s>īryāpatha</s>) — this is called bodily morality.

body.text: 4 | udgṛhṇanvākśīlaṃ sākalyena prajahāti mṛṣāvādaṃ paiśunyaṃ pāruṣyaṃ sambhinnapralāpam | na kadāpi pratārayati na ca saṃgatānbhinatti nābhyākhyāti na ca kṛtrimāṃ vācamudāharati nāpi lokāprāsādakamupāyamāracayati bhāṣate viśvastaṃ madhuramakapaṭaṃ bhāṣate nityahitam | śikṣayati kuśalamācaritumityucyate vākśīlam ||
body.translated_text: 4. Taking up verbal morality, one completely abandons false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), slander (<s>paiśunya</s>), harsh speech (<s>pāruṣya</s>), and idle chatter (<s>sambhinnapralāpa</s>). One never deceives, does not divide those who are united, does not accuse falsely, does not utter artificial speech, and does not devise methods that displease people. One speaks what is trustworthy, sweet, and without deceit. One speaks what is always beneficial. One trains [others] to practice the wholesome — this is called verbal morality.

body.text: 5 | udgṛhṇaṃścittaśīlaṃ niruṇaddhi lobhadveṣamithyādṭaṣṭīḥ | nityaṃ vidadhāti mṛducittam | nātyayānācarati | śraddhadhāti pāpakarmaṇāmaśūbhaṃ phalaṃ bhavatīti bhavanābalena nāśubhānyacarati | kṣudreṣvapi pāreṣu janayati gurutara (pāpa)saṃjñām | ajñānataḥ kurvanpāpāni vibheti paścāttatpatte sattveṣu notpādayati dveṣam | dṭaṣṭvā sattvānutpādayati snehacittam | kṛtaṃ jānāti pratyupakaropyavimatsaracittaḥ | puṇyācaraṇe chandaṃ janayan nityaṃ śikṣayati janān | nityaṃbhāvayati maitrīcittam | karuṇāyatesarveṣvityucyate cittaśīlam ||
body.translated_text: 5. Taking up mental morality, one restrains greed (<s>lobha</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). One always maintains a gentle mind. One does not commit transgressions. One has faith that unwholesome fruits result from sinful actions, and through the power of this contemplation, one does not perform unwholesome deeds. Even in minor faults, one generates the perception of extremely grave sin. When committing faults through ignorance, one is afraid afterward; when [the fault] comes to light, one does not generate hatred toward beings. Seeing beings, one generates a mind of affection. One acknowledges what has been done [for one] and reciprocates without a jealous mind. Generating enthusiasm for meritorious conduct, one always trains people. One always cultivates a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). One is compassionate (<s>karuṇā</s>) toward all — this is called mental morality.

body.text: 6 | eteṣāṃ daśakuśalakarmapathānāṃ paṃcākāro lābhaḥ nigṛhyate duścaritamiti prathamaḥ | utpadyate kuśalacittamiti dvitīyaḥ | nirudhyante kleśā iti tṛtīyaḥ | paripūryate viśuddhacittamiti caturthaḥ | samedhate śīlamiti paṃcamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 6. The gain from these ten wholesome paths of action (<s>daśakuśalakarmapatha</s>) has five aspects: first, misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>) is restrained; second, a wholesome mind arises; third, the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are ceased; fourth, a purified mind is fulfilled; fifth, morality (<s>śīla</s>) flourishes.

body.text: 7 | kuśalamacaranpuruṣo na carati cetpramādamadhigacchati samyaksmṛtim | vivinakti kuśalākuśalam | jñātavyamevaṃvidhaḥ prabhavati puruṣo dhruvamācarituṃ daśakuśalakarmāṇi | caturaśītisahasrāṇyamprameyāṇi śīlāṅgāni daśakuśaleṣveva śīleṣvantarbhavanti | santīmāni daśakuśalaśīlāni sarvakuśalaśīlamūlāni | prahāṇātkāyavākcittaśūbhānāṃ nirodhātsarvākuśaladharmāṇāmucyate śīlamiti ||
body.translated_text: 7. A person who practices the wholesome, who does not act heedlessly when [not practicing], attains right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>). One who discriminates the wholesome from the unwholesome — it should be known that such a person surely has the capacity to practice the ten wholesome actions. The eighty-four thousand immeasurable limbs of morality are all included within these ten wholesome moralities. These ten wholesome moralities are the root of all wholesome morality. Through the abandonment of unwholesome [actions] of body, speech, and mind, and through the cessation of all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — this is called morality (<s>śīla</s>).

body.text: 8 | śīlaṃ paṃcavidham | prathamaṃ prātimokṣaśīlam | dvitīyaṃ dhyānasahacaraśīlam | tṛtīyamanāsravaśīlam | caturthamindriyadamanaśīlam | paṃcamamavijñaptiśīlam | caturudīritajñaptikarmaṇopādhyādavāptamucyate prātimokṣaśīlam | caturmauladhyānacaturasamāpattidhyānamucyate dhyānaśīlam | maulacaturdhyānaprathamadhyānāsamāpattirucyate 'nāsravaśīlam | damannindriyāṇi vidadhāti samyaksmṛticittam | paśyañchṛṇvanbudhyañjānabrū paśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni notpādayatyasaṃprajanyamityucyata indriyadamanaśīlam | utsṛjatyātmabhāvamanāgate 'dhvanyakartuṃ punaraśubhamityucyate 'vijñaptiśīlam|
body.translated_text: 8. Morality (<s>śīla</s>) is fivefold: first, <s>prātimokṣa</s> morality (individual liberation vows); second, morality accompanied by <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation); third, uncontaminated morality (<s>anāsravaśīla</s>); fourth, morality of sense-faculty restraint (<s>indriyadamana</s>); fifth, non-manifest morality (<s>avijñaptiśīla</s>). [Morality] obtained from a preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) through the fourfold expressed motion-act (<s>jñaptikarma</s>) is called <s>prātimokṣa</s> morality. The four fundamental <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and the four formless attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) are called <s>dhyāna</s> morality. The first <s>dhyāna</s> attainment among the four fundamental <s>dhyānas</s> is called uncontaminated morality (<s>anāsravaśīla</s>). Taming the sense faculties (<s>indriya</s>) [means] maintaining right mindfulness and mental [composure]; seeing, hearing, cognizing, and knowing forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangible objects, one does not generate lack of clear comprehension (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>) — this is called morality of sense-faculty restraint. Relinquishing one's own existence in the future so as not to perform unwholesomeness again — this is called non-manifest morality (<s>avijñaptiśīla</s>).

body.text: 9 | bodhisattva ācarati śīlaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhāveṇikam | aveṇikatvāducyate kuśalaśīlagrahaṇam | kuśalaśīlagrahaṇatvātkaroti sarvasattvāṃllābhinaḥ gṛhṇan maitrīcittaśīlaṃ paritrāyate sukhayituṃ sattvān | gṛhṇan karuṇācittaśīlaṃ kṣamate sarvaduḥkhānyuddhartuṃ vipattiḥ | gṛhṇanmuditācittaśīlaṃ nandatyakuśīdatvācca kuśalānyācarati | gṛhṇannupekṣācittaśīlaṃ śavumitrayorbhavatiu samaḥ parihartuṃ rāgadveṣam | gṛhṇāti dānaśīlaṃ śikṣayituṃ sāntvayituṃ ca sarvasattvāt | gṛhṇan kṣāntiśīlaṃ bhavati nityaṃ mṛducitto dveṣāvaraṇabaprahīṇatvāt | gṛhṇanvīryaśīlaṃ vardhayati pratidinaṃ kuśalakarmāṇyapratinivartanāt | gṛhṇanśyānaśīlaṃ prajahāti rāgamakuśalaṃ vardhayitudhyānāṅḥāni | gṛhṇan prajñāśīlaṃ bahu śṛṇoti kuśalamūlaṃ (tatprati) atṛpteḥ | gṛhṇāti kalyāṇamitrasaṃgrahaśīlaṃ paripūrayituṃ bodhimanuttaraṃ mārgam | gṛhṇātyakalyāṇabhitraparityāgaśīlaṃ parityaktuṃ trividhaṃ duścaritamaṣṭau bhayasthānānī ||
body.translated_text: 9. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) that is unshared with <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas). Because it is unshared, it is called the grasping of wholesome moral conduct (<s>kuśalaśīla</s>). Through the grasping of wholesome moral conduct, one benefits all beings. Grasping the moral conduct of a mind of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), one rescues [beings] in order to bring them happiness. Grasping the moral conduct of a mind of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), one endures [all hardships] in order to lift [beings] out of all sufferings and calamities. Grasping the moral conduct of a mind of <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), one rejoices and, through non-idleness, practices wholesome [deeds]. Grasping the moral conduct of a mind of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), one is equal toward foes and friends, in order to abandon attachment and aversion. One grasps the moral conduct of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), in order to train and soothe all beings. Grasping the moral conduct of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), one is always of a gentle mind, because the obstruction of hatred has been abandoned. Grasping the moral conduct of <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), one increases wholesome actions day by day, through non-regression. Grasping the moral conduct of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), one abandons unwholesome attachment (<s>rāga</s>), in order to increase the limbs of meditation (<s>dhyānāṅga</s>). Grasping the moral conduct of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), one listens extensively [to teachings], from insatiability regarding roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). One grasps the moral conduct of gathering virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), in order to fulfill the unsurpassed path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). One grasps the moral conduct of abandoning evil friends (<s>akalyāṇamitra</s>), in order to abandon the three kinds of misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>) and the eight occasions of fear (<s>bhayasthāna</s>).

body.text: 10 | bodhisattvo gṛhṇanpariśuddhaśīlaṃ na pratiṣṭhito bhavati kāmadhātau na ca rūpadhātau nāpi ca pratiṣṭhito bhavatyarūpadhātāviti pariśuddhaśīlam | pariharati rāgarajāsyapanayati dveṣāvagṇaṃ niruṇaddhyavidyāvaraṇamiti pariśuddhaśīlam | parihārati dvāvantau śāśvatam cocchedaṃ cāpratilaumahetupratyayeneti pariśuddhaśīlam| na spṛśati rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni prajñaptilakṣaṇānīti pariśuddhaśīlam | na badhnāti hetau notpādayati dṭaṣṭīrna pratiṣṭhāpayati vicikitsākaukṛtye iti pariśuddhaśīlam | na pratiṣṭhāpayati rāgadveṣamohāstrīṇyakuśalamūlānīti pariśuddhaśīlam | na pratiṣṭhāpayatyātmamānaṃ madamānamabhimānaṃ mānātimānaṃ mahāmānaṃ mṛduḥ kuśalasnigdho bhavatīti pariśuddhaśīlam | neñjati lābhālābhanindāpraśaṃsāyaśo 'yaśasukhaduḥkheṣu nānulipyate lokasatye śūnye prajñatau bhavati cānugataḥ paramārthasatyamiti pariśuddhaśīlam | akleśamaparitāpaṃ śāntaṃ vimuktilakṣaṇamidaṃśīlam | saṃkṣepata ucyate kāyajīvita nirapekṣo 'nityasaṃjñādarśanenotpādayati vairāgyaṃ sodyogaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ bhāvayannabhyutsāhena vīryamācaratīti pariśūddhaśīlam | bodhisattvasya śīlamācarato na bhavati pariśūddhacittadṭaṣṭiḥ saṃjñāvimuktihetoritīyaṃ śīlapāramitā ||
body.translated_text: 10. A <s>Bodhisattva</s>, grasping pure moral conduct (<s>pariśuddhaśīla</s>), is not established in the desire realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>), nor in the form realm (<s>rūpadhātu</s>), nor is he established in the formless realm (<s>arūpadhātu</s>) — this is pure moral conduct. He removes the dust of attachment (<s>rāgarajas</s>), destroys the fire of aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), and blocks the obstruction of ignorance (<s>avidyāvaraṇa</s>) — this is pure moral conduct. He avoids the two extremes — eternalism (<s>śāśvata</s>) and annihilationism (<s>uccheda</s>) — through cause and condition that do not go against [the middle way] — this is pure moral conduct. He does not touch form (<s>rūpa</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), which have the characteristics of mere designation (<s>prajñapti</s>) — this is pure moral conduct. He does not bind [himself] to causes, does not generate views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), and does not establish doubt and remorse (<s>vicikitsā-kaukṛtya</s>) — this is pure moral conduct. He does not establish greed, hatred, and delusion — the three unwholesome roots (<s>akuśalamūla</s>) — this is pure moral conduct. He does not establish self-conceit (<s>ātmamāna</s>), intoxicating pride (<s>madamāna</s>), false pride (<s>abhimāna</s>), excessive pride (<s>mānātimāna</s>), or great pride (<s>mahāmāna</s>); he is gentle, wholesome, and smooth — this is pure moral conduct. He is not moved by gain and loss, blame and praise, fame and disrepute, happiness and suffering; he is not tainted by worldly truth and, being an expert in emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>), he follows the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>) — this is pure moral conduct. Free from affliction, free from torment, peaceful, having the characteristic of liberation (<s>vimukti</s>) — this is [pure] moral conduct. In brief, it is said: without regard for body and life, through the perception of impermanence (<s>anityasaṃjñā</s>), one generates dispassion; with effort one cultivates roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) and with enthusiasm practices vigor — this is pure moral conduct. For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who practices moral conduct, there is no view of a pure mind, because of the condition of perception and liberation — this is the <s>śīlapāramitā</s> (perfection of moral conduct).

body.text: (iti bodhicittātpādasuitraśāstre śīlapāramitā nāma paṃcamo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the fifth chapter named '<s>Śīlapāramitā</s>' [the Perfection of Moral Conduct] [is concluded].)

body.text: ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Sixth Chapter

body.text: kṣāntipāramitā
body.translated_text: <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (The Perfection of Patience)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathamācarati kṣāntim | kṣāntirātmaparobhayalābhāya cedevaṃvidhā kṣāntirniṣpādayati bodhimārgam | bodhisattvaḥ kāmayate vinetuṃ sattvānaparhartuṃ duḥkhānyācarati tasmātkṣāntim | kṣāntimācarataścitaṃ vinītaṃ bhavati | sattvānāmupekṣate balavanmadamānaṃ (svayaṃ) na cācarati | paśyantudvṛttānutpādayati karuṇām | mṛdulamudīrayandeśayati kuśalacaryām | vibhajya darśayati yo dvepo yā ca kṣāntiryaśca tayorvipāka itīdaṃ bodhisattvasyādikṣānticittam ||
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice <s>kṣānti</s> (patience)? If patience benefits oneself, others, and both — then such patience accomplishes the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva</s> desires to tame beings and remove their sufferings; therefore he practices patience. For one who practices patience, the mind becomes tamed. He overlooks the strong pride (<s>madamāna</s>) of beings and does not [himself] practice it. Seeing the ill-conducted, he generates compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). Gently encouraging [them], he teaches the practice of virtue. He distinguishes and shows what hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) is, what patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) is, and what the ripening (<s>vipāka</s>) of each is — this is the initial mind of patience of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: 2 | kṣāntyācaraṇahetoḥ pāpakaṃ vidurī bhavati | kāyacittaṃ praśāntaṃ bhavatītyasyātmalābhaḥ | vinayati sattvānanuvartate sarvāniti paralābhaḥ | caritvā mahatīmanuttarāṃ kṣānti sattveṣu pariṇāmyātmanā salābhinaḥ karotītyubhayalābhaḥ | kṣānticaryāhetorlabhate janamataṃ yāvallabhate buddhasya śobhanottamāni lakṣaṇānuvyañjanānīti niṣpādayati bodhimārgam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Through the practice of patience, evil (<s>pāpaka</s>) is kept at a distance. The body and mind become peaceful — this is one's own benefit (<s>ātmalābha</s>). One tames beings and follows them all — this is the benefit of others (<s>paralābha</s>). Having practiced great and unsurpassed patience, one dedicates [the merit] to beings, making them partakers of the benefit along with oneself — this is the benefit of both (<s>ubhayalābha</s>). Through the practice of patience, one gains the approval of people, and eventually attains the excellent and supreme marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and minor characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s> — thus one accomplishes the path of awakening.

body.text: 3 | kṣāntistrividhā | tadyathā kāyakṣāntirvākkṣānti rmanaḥkṣāntiśceti | kā nāma kāyakṣāntiḥ | yadi kaścanākrośati nindati tāḍayati yāvatāharati tatsarvaṃ kṣamate | paśyansattvānatrāṇe bhaye ca vyatiharati tairātmānaṃ na ca śrāmyatīti kāyakṣāntiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 3. <s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) is of three kinds, namely: bodily patience (<s>kāyakṣānti</s>), verbal patience (<s>vākkṣānti</s>), and mental patience (<s>manaḥkṣānti</s>). What is bodily patience? If someone abuses, reviles, strikes, or even carries one away — one endures all of that. Seeing beings without protection and in fear, one exchanges oneself with them and does not grow weary — this is bodily patience.
