body.text: 4 | kā nāma vākkṣāntiḥ | ākrośakaṃ paśyanna pratyākrośati niḥśabdaṃ kṣamate | ākośakamakāraṇamapyupagataṃ vilokayanmadhurayā girā sampratīcchati | mṛpaiva dūṣyamāṇo nirnimittamabhyākhyātaḥ sarvaṃ kṣamata iti vākkṣāntiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 4. What is verbal patience? Seeing one who abuses, one does not abuse in return but silently endures. Seeing an abuser who has approached even without cause, one receives him with sweet speech. Even when being falsely accused and denounced without reason, one endures all — this is verbal patience.

body.text: 5 | kā nāma manaḥkṣānti | dveṣiṇamavalokayannodgṛhṇāti dvepacitaṃ kopito na vikarotyātmacittam | nindāpakīrtiṣvati citte bhavati nivaira iti manaḥkṣānti ||
body.translated_text: 5. What is mental patience? Observing one who is hostile, one does not take up accumulated hatred. When angered, one does not disturb one's own mind. In the face of blame and infamy, the mind remains without enmity — this is mental patience.

body.text: 6 | tāḍitaṃ jagati dvividham | ucitamanucittaṃ ca | satyaparādhe saṃdihānena kena cijjanena tāḍitaḥ kṣametāmṛtamivodgṛhṇīyādādaramutpādayettāḍayitari | kasmāt | sādhu śīlaṃ śikṣayanmāṃ cikitsati pāpādapanayati | yadyanucitameva māmapakaroti māmapahanti tadā cintayenna kṛto mayāparādho 'tītakarmaṇāmevaitatkāritaṃ tena soḍhavyameca | punarevaṃ vibhāvayedyatvāri bhūtānīmāni pañcaskaṃghapratyayairabhisaṃhatāni yāni tāḍayante tāḍayanti ca | punarevaṃ paśyedyatsa puruṣo 'jña ivonmatta iveti mayā karuṇāyitavyaṃ kimuta na kṣantavyam ||
body.translated_text: 6. Being struck in the world is of two kinds: deserved and undeserved. When struck by someone who is in doubt about a real offense, one should endure it, receive it like ambrosia, and generate respect toward the one who strikes. Why? Because 'he heals me well, training me in moral conduct and removing me from evil.' If he harms me undeservedly, if he injures me, then one should reflect: 'I have committed no offense; this is caused by past actions alone, therefore it must be endured.' Furthermore, one should contemplate thus: 'These four elements, compounded by the conditions of the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), are what strike and are what are struck.' Furthermore, one should see thus: 'That person is like an ignorant one, like a madman — I should feel compassion for him; how much more should I practice patience!'

body.text: 7 | ākrośo dvividhaḥ | ucito 'nucitaśca | ucitamuktaṃ cenmayāpatraptavyam | anucitamuktaṃ cenmavā na kiṃcidapi kartavyam | dhavaniriva vāyuriva cātigacchannāpakaroti māmiti soḍhavyam | dviṣṭo 'pyevameva soḍhavyaḥ | kupito mayi mayā soḍhavyaḥ | ahaṃ cettaṃ pratikupyeyaṃ durgatimadhigaccheyamanāgate 'dhvani vedayeyaṃ mahāduḥkham | pratyayairebhirmama kāyaścedbhidyeta viśīryeta mayā notpādanīyo dvepaḥ | pratyayānāmatītakarmaṇāmetaditi gambhīraṃ pratyavekṣaṇīyam karūṇācaraṇīyā maitrī ca | karuṇāyitavyaṃ sarveṣu | yadyehaṃ na prabhavāmyevamalpamapi duḥkhaṃ soḍhuṃ na ca śaknomi damayituṃ svacittaṃ tatkathamahaṃ prabhaviṣyāmi vinetuṃ sattvānvimocayituṃ sarvānakuśaladharmānpūrayitumanuttaraṃ phalam ||
body.translated_text: 7. Verbal abuse is of two kinds: deserved and undeserved. If what is said is deserved, one should feel ashamed. If what is said is undeserved, one should not do anything [in response]. Like a sound, like the wind, it passes by and does not harm me — thus it should be endured. Even one who is hostile should be endured in the same way. When angered toward me, I should endure it. If I were to be angered in return, I would reach a lower destiny (<s>durgati</s>) and in the future would experience great suffering. Even if through these conditions my body were to be broken apart and destroyed, I should not generate hatred. One should deeply contemplate: 'These conditions are from past actions.' One should practice <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion) and <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). One should feel compassion toward all. If I am not able to endure even such small suffering, and cannot tame my own mind, then how shall I be able to discipline beings, to liberate all from unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and to fulfill the supreme fruit?

body.text: 8 | yo hi dhīmānsukhena kṣāntimācarati labhate sa ākāravaiśiṣṭyam | bahudhanau bhavati janāstamavalokya muditā bhavanti sukhitāśca bhavanti sukhitāśca bhavanti mānayantyanu vartante ca | puruṣaṃ cedvikalāṅgaṃ paśyedvībhatsadarśanaṃ vikalendriyamakiñcanaṃ jāniyāttadidaṃ dvepapratyayaiḥ kāritam | ebhiḥ pratyayai dhīṃmānācaredgambhīrāṃ kṣāntim ||
body.translated_text: 8. Indeed, one who is wise and practices patience with ease obtains distinction of bearing. One becomes wealthy, and people seeing that person become joyful and happy, and they honor and follow [that person]. If one were to see a person who is maimed, of repulsive appearance, with defective faculties, and destitute — one should know that this was caused by the conditions of hatred. Through these conditions, the wise one should practice profound patience.

body.text: 9 | kṣāntyutpādapratyayasya santīmāni daśa vastūni | ātmani nātmalakṣaṇaṃ paśyatīti prathamam | na jātimedaṃ manasi karotīti dvitīyam | pratinivartate madamānāditi tṛtīyam | apakurvantaṃ na pratyayakarotīti caturtham | anityalakṣaṇaṃ paśyatīti paṃcamam | maitrī karuṇā cācaratīti ṣaṣṭham | na cittena pramādyatīti sanamam | upekṣate kṣutpipāsāduḥkhaduḥkhādīnītyaṣṭamam | dvepaṃ prajahātīti navamam | prajñā bhāvayatīti daśamam | puruṣaścedimāni pūrayati daśa vastṛmi jñātavyaṃ śaknoti sa puruṣaḥ kṣāntimācaritum ||
body.translated_text: 9. There are ten things that serve as conditions for the arising of patience: First, one sees no mark of self in oneself. Second, one does not bear in mind [distinctions of] birth. Third, one turns away from pride and arrogance. Fourth, one does not retaliate against one who does harm. Fifth, one sees the mark of impermanence. Sixth, one practices <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). Seventh, one does not become heedless in mind. Eighth, one remains equanimous toward hunger, thirst, suffering, and the like. Ninth, one abandons hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>). Tenth, one cultivates <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). If a person fulfills these ten things, it should be known that that person is able to practice patience.

body.text:
10 | bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pariśuddhāyāṃ yadācarati caramāyāṃ kṣāntau praviśate śūnyatāmalakṣaṇamapraṇihitamasaṃskṛtam | na ca dṭaṣṭijñānapraṇihitasaṃskṛtaiḥ saṃpariṣvakto bhavati nāpi ca śūnyatālakṣaṇāpraṇihitāsaṃskṛteṣu rajyati | dṛṣṭijñānapraṇihitasaṃskṛtaṃ sarvamevaśūnyamityevaṃvidhā kṣāntiradvayalakṣaṇā pariśuddhā caramā kṣāntirityucyate |
yadi viśati saṃyojanaparikṣayaṃ yadi viśati śāntaṃ nirvāṇamasaṃpṛktajātimaraṇaṃ na cāsya rāgo bhavati saṃyojanakṣaye na ca śānte na nirvāṇe | saṃyojanajātijarāmaraṇaṃ sarvaṃ śūnyamityevaṃvidhā kṣāntiradvayalakṣaṇā pariśuddhā caramā kṣāntirityucyate |
bhāvo na svato jāyate na parato jāyate na dvābhyāṃ jāyate | api ca nāstyupādo na cocchedo na ca vināśo na cāvināśo na kṣaya ityevaṃvidhā kṣāntiradvayalakṣaṇā pariśuddhā caramā kṣāntirityucyate |
na kṛtākṛtaṃ nāsaṃgo na bhedo na niṣpattirna caryā notpādavīryaṃ na karaṇotpāda ityevaṃvidhā kṣāntiranutpādakṣāntiḥ | bodhisattvo yadācaratyevaṃvidhāṃ kṣānti labhate vyākaraṇakṣāntim | bodhisattva ācarati kṣāntiṃ bhāvalakṣaṇaśūnyatāṃ sattvābhāvahetaustataḥ pūrayāte kṣāntipāramitām ||
body.translated_text:
10. When a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> practices the purified, final patience, he enters emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). He is not embraced by views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), wishes (<s>praṇihita</s>), or the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>), nor does he become attached to emptiness, signlessness, wishlessness, or the unconditioned. Views, knowledge, wishes, and the conditioned — all are indeed empty: such patience, having the characteristic of non-duality (<s>advayalakṣaṇā</s>), is called purified, final patience.
If one enters the complete destruction of fetters (<s>saṃyojanaparikṣaya</s>), if one enters peaceful <s>nirvāṇa</s> free from the conjunction of birth and death — and yet one has no attachment to the destruction of fetters, nor to peace, nor to <s>nirvāṇa</s>; fetters, birth, aging, and death — all are empty: such patience, having the characteristic of non-duality, is called purified, final patience.
Existence (<s>bhāva</s>) is not born from itself, not born from another, not born from both. Moreover, there is no arising, no cutting off, no destruction, no non-destruction, no decay: such patience, having the characteristic of non-duality, is called purified, final patience.
Neither made nor unmade, no non-attachment, no differentiation, no accomplishment, no practice, no arising-energy, no cause-of-arising: such patience is the patience of non-arising (<s>anutpādakṣānti</s>). When a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices such patience, he obtains the patience of being given a prediction (<s>vyākaraṇakṣānti</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices patience in the emptiness of the characteristics of existence, on account of the non-existence of beings — thereby he fulfills the perfection of patience (<s>kṣāntipāramitā</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre kṣāntipāramitā māna ṣaṣṭho vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the Perfection of Patience [<s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s>], the sixth chapter.)

body.text: saptamo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Seventh Chapter

body.text:
vīryapāramitā
1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathamācarati vīryam | vīryamātmaparobhayalābhāyacedevaṃvidhaṃ vīryaṃ niṣpādayati bodhimārgam | bodhisattvaḥ kāmayate vinetuṃ sattvānāparhatuṃ duḥkhānyācarati tasmādvīryam | vīryamācaransarvādhvasu sarvadotsāhacaryayā saṃgṛhṇāti pariśūddhaṃ brahmacaryaṃ pariharati kausīdyaṃ na ca cittena pramādyati | kṛcchreṣvahitāpakṣavastuṣu sarvadāsya vīryavattayā cittaṃ nāntataḥ pratyāvartata iti bodhisattvasyādi vīryacittam ||
body.translated_text:
The Perfection of Energy (<s>Vīryapāramitā</s>)
1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice energy (<s>vīrya</s>)? If energy is for the benefit of self, others, and both, such energy accomplishes the path to awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva</s> desires to discipline beings and remove [their] sufferings, and therefore practices energy. Practicing energy in all times, always with zealous conduct, he gathers pure holy conduct (<s>brahmacarya</s>), abandons laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), and does not become heedless in mind. In hardships and unfavorable matters, through his energy his mind never ultimately turns back — this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s initial energy-mind.

body.text: 2 | vīryācaraṇena labhate lokacaraṃ lokottaramanuttaraṃ saddharmamityasyātmalābhaḥ | śikṣayati sattvānyenācaraṃtyabhyutsāhena kuśalamiti paralābhaḥ | caritvā bodheḥ samyaghetuṃ sattveṣu pariṇāmyātmanā salābhinaḥ karotītyubhayalābhaḥ | vīryacaryāhetorlabhate paramapariśuddhaṃ satphalamatikramya ca bhūmī ryāvacchīghraṃ pūrayati sambodhimiti niṣpādayati bodhimārgam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Through the practice of energy, one obtains the worldly, supramundane, and unsurpassed true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) — this is one's own benefit (<s>ātmalābha</s>). One trains beings so that they practice zeal for the wholesome — this is the benefit of others (<s>paralābha</s>). Having practiced the right cause of awakening, transferring [the merit] to beings, one makes them share in the gain — this is the benefit of both (<s>ubhayalābha</s>). Through the cause of practicing energy, one obtains the supreme, perfectly pure, true fruit, surpasses the stages, and quickly fulfills perfect awakening (<s>sambodhi</s>) — thus one accomplishes the path to awakening.

body.text: 3 | vīryaṃ dvividham | gavepayatyanuttaraṃ mārgamiti prathamam | paritrātuṃ duḥkhādvipulābhilāpeṇa vīryaṃ janayatīti dvitīyam | pūrayanbodhisattvo daśānusmṛtīrutpādayati bodhicittam | ācarati vīryam | kā daśānusmṛtayaḥ | prathamā buddhānusmṛtiraprameyapuṇyā | dvitīyā dharmānusmṛtiracintyavimuktiḥ | tṛtīyā saṃghānusmṛtiḥ pariśuddhatayā niṣkalaṃkā | caturthī mahāmaitryanusmṛtiḥ sattvavyavasthāpanāya | paṃcamīmahākaruṇānusmṛtirduḥkhataḥ paritrāṇāya | ṣaṣṭhī samyaksamādhiskandhānusmṛtiranurocayituṃ kuśalācaraṇāya | saptamī mithyāsamādhiskandhānusmṛtiruddhartuṃ (sattvān kuśala-)mūlaṃ pratyānayanaya | aṣṭamī pretānusmṛtiḥ kṣutpipāsoṣṇatākleśamayī | navamī tiryaganusmṛti dīrghaduḥkhavedanātmikā | daśamī narakānusmṛtirdāhanabharjanavedanātmikā | bodhisattva evaṃ bhāvayati daśānusmṛtīstriratnapuṇyāni | bhāvayeyamahaṃ samyaksamādhi maitrī karuṇāṃ (tatra) sattvānārocayeyamahaṃ mṛṣā dhyāyatastridurgatiduḥkhāduddhareyaṃ nityamahaṃ parirakṣayeyamityevaṃ cintayati | saṃcintayannavikṣitaṃ divānaktaṃ bhāvayati sotsāhaṃ na ca viśrāmyatīti samyaksmṛtitā vīryaṃ samudeti ||
body.translated_text: 3. Vigor (<s>vīrya</s>) is twofold: first, seeking the unsurpassed path; second, generating vigor through extensive discourse for rescuing [beings] from suffering. Fulfilling [this], the <s>bodhisattva</s> generates <s>bodhicitta</s> by arousing the ten recollections (<s>daśānusmṛti</s>) and practices vigor. What are the ten recollections? First, recollection of the <s>Buddha</s> (<s>buddhānusmṛti</s>), of immeasurable merit. Second, recollection of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmānusmṛti</s>), which is inconceivable liberation. Third, recollection of the <s>Saṅgha</s> (<s>saṃghānusmṛti</s>), stainless through purity. Fourth, recollection of great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), for establishing beings. Fifth, recollection of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), for rescuing from suffering. Sixth, recollection of the aggregate of right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhiskandha</s>), to delight in and practice the wholesome. Seventh, recollection of the aggregate of wrong concentration (<s>mithyāsamādhiskandha</s>), to lift up [beings] and bring them back to the roots of wholesomeness. Eighth, recollection of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), [whose existence] consists of hunger, thirst, heat, and afflictions. Ninth, recollection of animals (<s>tiryak</s>), whose nature consists of long-lasting painful sensation. Tenth, recollection of the hells (<s>naraka</s>), whose nature consists of the sensations of burning and scorching. The <s>bodhisattva</s> contemplates thus — the ten recollections, the merits of the Three Jewels: 'May I cultivate right concentration, loving-kindness, and compassion; may I awaken beings therein; may I rescue those dwelling in false meditation from the suffering of the three unfortunate destinies; may I always protect them' — thus he reflects. Reflecting without distraction, he cultivates day and night with enthusiasm and does not rest — thus through right mindfulness, vigor arises.

body.text: 4 | vīryaṃ puna rbodhisattvasya caturvidham | tathāhi | catuḥsamyakpradhāna [prahāṇa]mārgamācarato 'nutpannānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ punaranutpādaḥ | utpannānāṃ punarakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ śīghraṃ samprahāṇam | anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmupāyena samutpādaḥ | utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ paripūraṇaṃ saṃvarddhanaṃ ca | evaṃ bodhisattva ācarati catvāri samyakpradhānāni na ca viśrāmyatītyucyate vīryam |
body.translated_text: 4. Furthermore, the <s>bodhisattva</s>'s vigor is fourfold. For thus: practicing the path of the four right exertions (<s>catuḥsamyakpradhāna</s>): the non-arising of unarisen unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; the swift abandonment of arisen unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; the arising through skillful means of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; and the fulfillment and increase of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Thus the <s>bodhisattva</s> practices the four right exertions and does not rest — this is called vigor.

body.text: 5 | vīryaṃ kṣapayati sarvakleśadhātūnsampravardhayati bodheranuttarāyāḥ samyaghetum | kāyacittamahāduḥkhānyakhilānyapi sahamāno bodhisattvo 'vasthāpayitumamilapati sattvānna ca viśrāmyatītyucyate vīryam ||
body.translated_text: 5. Vigor destroys all the elements of affliction (<s>kleśadhātu</s>) and increases the right cause of unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). Enduring all the great sufferings of body and mind without exception, the <s>bodhisattva</s> strives to establish beings and does not rest — this is called vigor.

body.text: 6 | bodhisattvaḥ vigatakalmapo 'cāṭukuṭilaḥ paryavasitamithyāvīrya ācarati samyagvīryam | tathāhi | ācarati śraddhāṃ dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntiṃ dhyānaṃ prajñāṃ maitrī karuṇāṃ muditāmupekṣām | sābhilāṣaṃ karogyakaravaṃ kariṣyāmīti viśvastacittaḥ sarvadācarati vīryam | nānutāpo 'sya kuśaladharmeṣu | pradīptaśira iva paritrāyate sattvānna ca cittaṃ parāvartayatītyucyate vīryam ||
body.translated_text: 6. The <s>bodhisattva</s>, free from impurity, without flattery or crookedness, having concluded wrong vigor, practices right vigor. For thus: he practices faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). With eager mind, [thinking] 'I am doing, I have done, I shall do,' with a trusting mind, he always practices vigor. He has no regret regarding wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. As if his head were on fire, he rescues beings and does not turn his mind away — this is called vigor.

body.text: 7 | kāyajīvitanirapekṣo 'pi bodhisattvaḥ paritrātuṃ (sattvān) duḥkhebhyaḥ paripālayatuṃ saddharmaṃ kāyamapekṣate nopekṣata īryāpathaṃ sarvadā bhāvayituṃ kuśaladharmān | kuśaladharmācaraṇakāle na cittena kusīdo bhavati | kāyajīvitavidhāte 'pi dharmaṃ na parityajatīti bodhisattvo bodhimārgaṃ caransotsāhamācarati vīryam | kusīdaḥ puruṣo 'samartho naikakālaṃ sarvaṃ dadāti na ca śīlamudgṛṇāyi na ca kṣamate duḥkhāni na cācaratyabhyutsāhena vīryam | na ca samādhau smṛtisaṃprajanyacitto bhavati na ca kuśalākuśalaṃ vivinakti | tenocyate dhīryamupādāya ṣaṭpāramitāḥ saṃpravardhanta iti | bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ saṃpravardhayati ced vīryaṃ labhate 'cirāt samyaksaṃvodhim ||
body.translated_text: 7. The <s>bodhisattva</s>, though without regard for body and life, still looks after the body in order to rescue beings from sufferings and to protect the true <s>Dharma</s>, but does not cling to [bodily] deportment — always cultivating wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. At the time of practicing wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he is not lazy in mind. Even when life and body are in danger, he does not abandon the <s>Dharma</s> — thus the <s>bodhisattva</s>, walking the path of <s>bodhi</s>, practices vigor with enthusiasm. A lazy person is incapable: he does not give everything at one time, does not take up morality, does not endure sufferings, does not practice vigor with enthusiasm, does not have a mind of mindfulness and clear comprehension in concentration, and does not discriminate the wholesome from the unwholesome. Therefore it is said: 'Through vigor, the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) increase.' If a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> increases vigor, he attains supreme perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) before long.

body.text: 8 | bodhisattvo mahāniṣpattyutpādena punaścaturvidhaṃ vīryaṃ janayati | tanna prathamamutpādayati mahāniṣpattiṃ dvitīyaṃ saṃgṛhṇāti śūraṃgamaṃ tṛtīyamācarati kuśalamūlaṃ caturthaṃ vinayati sattvān | kathaṃ bodhisattvomahāniṣpattimutpādayati | jātimaraṇeṣu kṣamate 'sya cittaṃ na ca gaṇayati kalpasaṃkhyāmaprameyeṣvaparyanteṣu niyutakoṭiśatasahasragaṃgānadībālukāvadasaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣu buddhamārgamudgrahīṣyāmyaklāntacitta ityakusīdasya [mahā]niṣpattivīryam | bodhisattvaḥ saṃgṛhṇañchūraṃgamaṃ janayati vīryam trisāhasramahāsāhasro 'yaṃ lokadhātuḥ paripūrṇo 'nnineti draṣṭuṃ buddhaṃ śrotuṃ dharma sthāpayituṃ sattvānkuśaladharmeṣvatikrāmatyetamagniṃ vinetuṃ sattvān saṃpratiṣṭhāpayati cittaṃ mahākaruṇāyāmiti śūraṃgamavīryam | bodhisattva ācarankuśalaṃmūlaṃ janayati vīryam | utpāditāni sarvāṇi kuśalamūlāni pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripūrayituṃ sarvajñatāmiti kuśalamūlācaraṇavīryam | bodhisattvaḥ vinayansattvāñjanayati vīryam | aprameyāḥ sattvabhāvā aparyantā ākāśadhātusamā aparisaṃkhyeyāḥ | bodhisattvaḥ praṇidadhāti yannirvāpayitavyānte yathā na kaścanāvaśiṣyate | nirvāpayituṃ sotsāhamācarati vīryamiti [sattva-]vinayavīryam ||
body.translated_text: 8. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through the generation of great accomplishment (<s>mahāniṣpatti</s>), again generates fourfold vigor (<s>vīrya</s>). First, he generates the great accomplishment; second, he gathers heroic progress (<s>śūraṃgama</s>); third, he practices roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>); fourth, he disciplines beings. How does the <s>Bodhisattva</s> generate the great accomplishment? His mind endures through births and deaths and does not count the number of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) — in immeasurable, limitless, innumerable <s>kalpas</s> [as numerous as] the sands of hundreds of thousands of millions of <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, [thinking] 'I shall take up the <s>Buddha</s>-path with an unwearied mind' — this is the vigor of great accomplishment for one who is not lazy. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gathering heroic progress, generates vigor: this billion-world system (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) is filled with fire — to see the <s>Buddha</s>, hear the <s>Dharma</s>, establish beings in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he crosses through this fire to discipline beings and establishes his mind in great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) — this is the vigor of heroic progress. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, practicing roots of merit, generates vigor: he dedicates all the roots of merit he has generated to the unsurpassed perfect awakening, to fulfill omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) — this is the vigor of practicing roots of merit. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, disciplining beings, generates vigor: the realms of beings are immeasurable, limitless, equal to the realm of space, innumerable. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> vows that in bringing them to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, not a single one shall remain. He practices vigor with zeal to bring them to <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the vigor of disciplining beings.

body.text: 9 | saṃkṣepata ucyate | bodhisattvo bhāvayati mārgasahāyāṃ puṇyasahāyāmanuttarāṃ prajñām | saṃgṛhṇanbuddhadharmānutpādayati vīryam | aparyantā buddhaguṇāaprameyāḥ | bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahāniṣpatyutpādena janitaṃ vīryamapyeṣamaparyantamaprameyam | bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vīryamācarannaviraktacittobhavatyuddhartuṃ duḥkhānīti pūrayati vīryapāramitām ||
body.translated_text: 9. Stated briefly: the <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivates the unsurpassed <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) as a companion to the path and a companion to merit. Gathering the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, he generates vigor. The qualities of the <s>Buddha</s> are limitless and immeasurable. The vigor generated by the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> through the generation of great accomplishment is also limitless and immeasurable. The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, practicing vigor with a mind that does not weary of rescuing [beings] from sufferings, fulfills the perfection of vigor (<s>vīryapāramitā</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre vīryapāramitā māna saptamo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the seventh chapter, called 'The Perfection of Vigor (<s>Vīryapāramitā</s>),' [is concluded].)

body.text: aṣṭamo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Eighth Chapter

body.text: dhyāmapāramiatā
body.translated_text: The Perfection of Meditation (<s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathamāvarati dhyānam | dhyānamātmaparobhayalābhāya cedevaṃvidhaṃ dhyānaṃ niṣpādyati bodhimārgam | bodhisattvaḥ kāmayate vinetuṃ sattvānaparhatuṃ duḥkhānyacarati tasmāddhyānam | yogāvacaraḥ svacittaṃ saṃgṛhṇan sarvavikṣepaikhyavahito gacchantiṣṭhanniṣīdañchayāno vā smṛtimabhimukhīmupasthāpayati | paśyatyanulobhaṃ pratilobhaṃ kapālaṃ śīrṣa kaśerukāṃ bāhkurparamuraḥ parśakāṃ śroṇi kaṭaṃ jānvadharaṃ guṇau | anusmaratyānapānamiti bodhisattvasyādidhyānacittam ||
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> enter meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>)? If meditation is for the benefit of self, others, and both, one accomplishes such meditation [as] the path of awakening. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, desiring to discipline beings and remove sufferings, practices meditation for that reason. The practitioner of yoga (<s>yogāvacara</s>), restraining his own mind, heedful against all distractions, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, establishes mindfulness directed [inward]. He contemplates [the parts of the body]: the front of the torso, the back, the skull, the head, the vertebrae, the arms, the elbows, the chest, the ribs, the hips, the waist, the knees, the lower legs, and the ankles. He recollects the inhalation and exhalation (<s>ānāpāna</s>) — this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s initial meditation-mind.

body.text: 2 | dhyānacaryāhetorna prāpnotyakuśalāni sadāsya nandati cittamityasyātmalābhaḥ | vinayansattvānācārayati samyaksmṛtimiti paralābhaḥ | caritvā pariśuddhaṃ samādhiṃ vītākuśalavitarkavicāraḥ sattveṣu pariṇāmyātmanā salābhinaḥ karotītyubhayalābhaḥ | dhyānacaryā hetorlabhate 'ṣṭau vimokṣānyāvacchraraṃgamavajasamādhimiti niṣpādayati bodhimārgam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Through the practice of meditation, one does not attain the unwholesome and one's mind always rejoices — this is one's own benefit (<s>ātmalābha</s>). Disciplining beings, one teaches right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>) — this is the benefit of others (<s>paralābha</s>). Having practiced purified <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), free from unwholesome reasoning and investigation, dedicating it to beings, one makes oneself and others beneficiaries — this is the benefit of both (<s>ubhayalābha</s>). Through the practice of meditation, one attains the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭau vimokṣa</s>) up to the <s>śūraṅgamasamādhi</s> (heroic progress concentration) — thus one accomplishes the path of awakening.

body.text: 3 | dhyānaṃ tribhirdharmairupajāyate | ke vayaḥ | prathamaḥ śrutamayī prajñā | dvitīyaścintāmayī prajñā | tṛtīyo bhāvanāmayī prajñā | tribhirebhirdharmaiḥ krameṇopajāyante sarvasamādhayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 3. Meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) arises through three <s>dharmas</s>. What are they? The first is wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>). The second is wisdom born of reflection (<s>cintāmayī prajñā</s>). The third is wisdom born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>). Through these three <s>dharmas</s>, all <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) arise in sequence.

body.text: 4 | kā nāma śrutamayī prajñā | yathā yathā dharmāñcaṇoti tathā tathasya cittṃ prītaṃ bhavati sukhitam | punarevamanusmarati santyānantaryavimokṣādayo buddhadharmāḥ | ime dharmā bahuśratenāvāpyante | evamanusmmṛtya sarvadā dharmagaveṣaṇākāle 'syottarottasmutsāhaḥ saṃpravardhate 'horātraṃ dharmaśravaṇe 'syābhirucirbhavati na ca klāntirnāpyasyatuptiriti śrutamayī prajñā |
body.translated_text: 4. What is wisdom born of learning (<s>śrutamayī prajñā</s>)? As one hears more and more <s>dharmas</s>, one's mind becomes joyful and happy. Furthermore, one recollects thus: 'There are <s>Buddha-dharmas</s> such as the [eight] liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the [five] uninterrupted [concentrations] (<s>ānantarya</s>), and so forth. These <s>dharmas</s> are obtained through much learning.' Having thus recollected, at all times during the search for <s>Dharma</s>, one's zeal increases more and more; day and night one delights in hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, and one experiences neither weariness nor satiety — this is wisdom born of learning.

body.text: 5 | kā nāma cintāmayī prajñā | cintayati sarve saṃskṛtadharmāstathatālakṣaṇāḥ | tathā hi | anityā duḥkhāḥ śūnyā anātmāno 'śucayaḥ kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇamutpadyante nirudhyante 'ciraṃ pamohāgninā jvalitāḥ saṃvarddhayanti paścimaṃ duḥkhamahāskandham | māyāvanmṛṣeva bhāgha it sarveṣu saṃskṛtadharmeṣu janayati saṃvegam | samadhikotsāhaṃ gacchati buddhaprajñām | cinayati yattathāgatāprajñācintyāparimeyā mahābalāparājitā prāptāpagatabhayasparśāṃ mahānagarī na ca punarāvartate duḥkhebhyo 'prameyebhyaḥ sattvānaparitrāyate | evaṃ jānāti buddhasyāprameyāṃ praḥyāṃ paśyati saṃskṛtadharmāṇāmaparimeyadu| kāmayate gaveṣayitumanuttaraṃ mahāyānamiti cintāmayī pajñā ||
body.translated_text: 5. What is <s>cintāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born from reflection)? One reflects that all conditioned <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) bear the mark of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). For thus: they are impermanent, suffering, empty, without self, impure; they arise and cease moment by moment; before long, blazing with the fire of delusion, they increase the final great mass of suffering. Like an illusion, like a falsity, like a dream — generating urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>) toward all conditioned phenomena, one proceeds with increased vigor toward the wisdom of the <s>Buddha</s>. One reflects that the <s>prajñā</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is inconceivable, immeasurable, of great power, unconquered, having reached the great city free from the touch of fear, and does not return again; [they] rescue immeasurable beings from sufferings. Thus, knowing the immeasurable wisdom of the <s>Buddha</s> and seeing the immeasurable suffering of conditioned phenomena, one desires to seek the unsurpassed <s>Mahāyāna</s> — this is wisdom born from reflection.

body.text:
6 | kā nāma bhāvanāmayī prajñetyucyate | tyajati rāgamakuśalāṃśca dharmān | tenopajāyante 'sya vitarkavicāraprītisukhāni viśati prathamaṃ dhyānam | kṣapayato vitarkavicāran prasannabhyantarastaikāgracittasyāvitarkavicāraḥ samādhirasyopajāyate saprīti śukhaṃ viśati dvitīyaṃ dhyānam | prīti parityajyopekṣāsaṃskāravān smṛtisaṃprajanyacittaḥ kāye śukhaṃ vedayakṣāryābhilāpepekṣārhāṃ nityamanusmaransukhāṃ vedanāṃ viśati tṛtīyaṃ dhyānam prajahāti duḥkhaṃ prajahāti śukhaṃ niruṇaddhi śokaṃ prīti viśatyaduḥkhamśukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśūddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam |
atyetisarvaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam | niruṇaddhi sarvaṃ pratighalakṣaṇaṃ nānusmarati viṣabhāgalakṣaṇaṃ tena jānatyākāśamanantam | tataḥ praviśatyakāśamarūpadhyānāyatanam | atyeti sarvamākāśalakṣaṇaṃ tena jānāti vijñānamanantam | tatapraviśati vijñānamrūpadhyānāyatanam | atyeti sarvaṃ vijñānalakṣaṇaṃ tena jānātyākiṃcanyam | tena jānan nevasaṃjñānāsṃjñāsparśaṃ tataḥ praviśati naiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanam | sarvadharmānkevalamanusmarañcarati na ca rajyati gaveṣayatyanuttaraṃ mahāyānam | pūrayatyanuttarāṃ samyak sambodhimiti bhāvanāmayī praḥyā |
bodhisattvaḥ śrutena cintayā bhāvanayā ca saṃgṛhṇāti cittam | tataḥ pūrayati [ṣaḍ] abhijñā[stisro] vidyāḥ samādhi dhyānapāramitām ||
body.translated_text: 6. What is called <s>bhāvanāmayī prajñā</s> (wisdom born from meditation)? One abandons desire (<s>rāga</s>) and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Thereby there arise for one initial application (<s>vitarka</s>), sustained application (<s>vicāra</s>), rapture (<s>prīti</s>), and happiness (<s>sukha</s>) — one enters the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption). Eliminating initial and sustained application, with inner clarity and one-pointed mind, there arises a concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) without initial and sustained application, with rapture and happiness — one enters the second <s>dhyāna</s>. Abandoning rapture, endowed with equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) and formations, with a mind of mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>), experiencing happiness in the body, [as] the noble ones declare: 'one abides in equanimity,' always mindful of the pleasant feeling — one enters the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Abandoning suffering, abandoning happiness, suppressing grief and rapture, one enters the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — neither suffering nor happiness, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. One transcends all marks of form. One suppresses all marks of resistance. One does not attend to marks of diversity. Thereby one knows space to be infinite. Then one enters the formless meditative base of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>). Transcending all marks of space, one thereby knows consciousness to be infinite. Then one enters the formless meditative base of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>). Transcending all marks of consciousness, one thereby knows nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanya</s>). Knowing the contact of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñā</s>), one then enters the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Merely recollecting all <s>dharmas</s>, one practices without attachment and seeks the unsurpassed <s>Mahāyāna</s>. One fulfills the unsurpassed perfect awakening — this is wisdom born from meditation. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through hearing (<s>śruta</s>), reflection (<s>cintā</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), gathers the mind. Thereby one fulfills the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the three knowledges (<s>vidyā</s>), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and the <s>dhyānapāramitā</s> (perfection of meditation).

body.text: 7 | dhyāyanbodhisattvaḥ punarācarati daśadharmāñchrāvakapratyekabuddhāveṇikān | ke deśa | dhyāyannairātmyamavāpnoti tathāgatadhyānānīti prathamaḥ dhyānna ca sakto na ca rakto na ca bhavati kliṣṭacitto na ca gaveṣayatyātmasukhamiti dvitīyaḥ | dhyāyannavāpnotyuddhikarmāṇi pariḥyātuṃ sattvānāṃ cittacaryāmiti tṛtīyaḥ | dhyānprajānāti janakāyacittāni paritrāyate ca sarvasattvāniti caturthaḥ | dhyāyānnācarati mahākaruṇāṃ chinatti sattvānāṃ kleśagranthimiti paṃcamaḥ | dhyāyandhyānasamādhiṃ samyagjānāti prameśanirgamamatikrāmyati tridhātumiti ṣaṣṭaḥ | dhyāyannityamulabhate vaśitāmavāpnoti kuśaladharmāniti saptamaḥ | dhyāyañcitaṃ śāntaṃbhavati nirvṛttaṃ yānadvayasyātikrāmyati sarvāṇi dhyānānītyaṣṭamaḥ | dhyāyannityaṃ viśati prajñāṃ lokamatikramyāvapnoti tatpadamiti navamaḥ | dhyāyanpratiṣṭhāpayati saddharmaṃ nirantaraṃ saṃvarddhayati triratnaṃ yena bhavatyanucchinnamiti daśamaḥ | bhavati caivaṃvidhaṃ dhyāaṃ śrāvakapratyekabudhāvenīkam ||
body.translated_text: 7. The meditating <s>Bodhisattva</s> further practices ten <s>dharmas</s> that are distinct from <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary buddhas). What are these ten? First: meditating on selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), one attains the <s>dhyānas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Second: in meditation, one is neither attached nor impassioned, does not have a defiled mind, and does not seek one's own happiness. Third: meditating, one attains supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>) in order to understand the mental conduct of beings. Fourth: in meditation, one knows the minds of assemblies and rescues all beings. Fifth: meditating, one practices great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) and cuts the knot of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of beings. Sixth: meditating, one rightly knows the <s>dhyāna-samādhi</s> and the exit from the [meditative] attainment, transcending the three realms (<s>tridhātu</s>). Seventh: meditating, one always gains mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>) and attains wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Eighth: meditating, the mind becomes peaceful and brought to cessation, transcending both vehicles and all <s>dhyānas</s>. Ninth: meditating, one always enters into <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), transcending the world, and attains that state (<s>pada</s>). Tenth: meditating, one establishes the true <s>Dharma</s>, continuously increases the Three Jewels (<s>triratna</s>), so that they remain uninterrupted. Such meditation is distinct from that of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>.

body.text: 8 | jñātuṃ punaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kliṣṭacittāni saṃgṛhṇāti sarvadhyānasamādhidharmān cittasthairyaṃ vidhātuṃ | dhyāyānpratiṣṭhāpayati cittasamatāmityucyate dhyānam | evaṃ samatā hyānaṃ samaṃ śūnyatayākṣaṇatayāpraṇihitatayākriyayā | śūnyatā khalvalakṣaṇāpraṇihitākriyābhiḥ samā tena sattvā api samāḥ | yataḥ sattvāḥ | yataḥ sattvāḥ samāstena dharmā api samāḥ | iti viśatyevaṃvidhāṃ samatāmiti dhyānam ||
body.translated_text: 8. Furthermore, to know the afflicted minds of all beings, he gathers all the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) in order to establish stability of mind. Meditating, he establishes equanimity of mind — this is called <s>dhyāna</s>. For this equanimity is the sameness through <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>ākṣaṇatā</s> (signlessness), <s>apraṇihitatā</s> (wishlessness), and non-action. <s>Śūnyatā</s> is indeed equal with signlessness, wishlessness, and non-action; therefore beings too are equal. Since beings are equal, <s>dharmas</s> too are equal. Thus entering such equanimity is called <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: 9 | punarbodhisattvo lokamanucarannapi na ca bhavati lokasaktaḥ prajahātyaṣṭau lokadharmānvināśayati sarvagranthiṃ tyajati janāvāsaṃ rocate 'sya viviktāyatanam | evaṃ dhyānamācarataścittaṃ saṃpratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati prajahāti saṃsārakarmāṇi ||
body.translated_text: 9. Furthermore, though the <s>Bodhisattva</s> wanders through the world, he is not attached to the world. He abandons the eight worldly <s>dharmas</s> (<s>aṣṭau lokadharmāḥ</s>), destroys all fetters (<s>granthi</s>), renounces the household life, and delights in secluded places. Thus, for one practicing <s>dhyāna</s>, the mind becomes firmly established; he abandons the actions of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: 10 | punarbodhisattvasya dhyānamācarata ṛddhirbhavati prajñopāyo matiḥ kathaṃ bhavatyṛddhi kathaṃ prajñā | paśyati cedrūpalakṣaṇam śṛṇoti śabdaṃ jānāti paracittaṃ smaratyatītaṃ prāpnoti sarvabuddhalokadhātūntadasyārddhiḥ | rūpaṃ jānāti ced dharmasvabhāvaṃ jānāti śabdagaṃndharasaspraṣṭavyacittasaṃskārāḥ svabhāvālakṣaṇāḥ śāntāḥparinirvṛtāstriṣvadhvasu samā iti | ākāśalakṣaṇaṃ jānāti buddhalokadhātumapariprāptanirodhamitiprajñā | kathamupāyaḥ kaṃtha matiḥ | dhyānasamādhimanuviśannutpādayati mahāmaitrīṃ karuṇāṃ na jahāti prāṇidhānaṃ vajramiva bhavati cāsya cittamavalokayanbuddhalokadhātu niṣpādayati bodhimārgamityupāyaḥ | cittaṃ sarvathāsyabhavati śāntam | na cātmāna ca pudgala iti cintayati sarvadharmānmūlasvabhāvāvikṣepān | paśyati buddhalokadhātumākāśalakṣaṇam yanniṣpannaṃ tatpaśyati śāntaṃ nirvāṇamiti matiḥ |
body.translated_text: 10. Furthermore, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practicing <s>dhyāna</s>, there arise supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), and insight (<s>mati</s>). How does <s>ṛddhi</s> arise? How does <s>prajñā</s> arise? If he sees the characteristics of form, hears sounds, knows others' minds, remembers the past, and reaches all <s>Buddha</s>-fields (<s>buddhalokadhātu</s>) — that is his <s>ṛddhi</s>. If he knows form as the own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasvabhāva</s>), and knows that sound, smell, taste, tangible objects, mind, and mental formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are without inherent characteristics (<s>svabhāvālakṣaṇa</s>), peaceful, completely extinguished (<s>parinirvṛta</s>), and equal in the three time periods — if he knows the characteristic of space and knows the <s>Buddha</s>-fields as unattained cessation (<s>apariprāptanirodha</s>) — that is <s>prajñā</s>. How is <s>upāya</s>? How is <s>mati</s>? Entering <s>dhyāna</s> and <s>samādhi</s>, he generates great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>), does not abandon compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), and his vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) becomes like a <s>vajra</s>. Observing the <s>Buddha</s>-fields, he accomplishes the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>) — this is <s>upāya</s>. His mind in all ways becomes peaceful. He does not conceive of self (<s>ātman</s>) or person (<s>pudgala</s>). He sees all <s>dharmas</s> as root own-nature without distraction (<s>mūlasvabhāvāvikṣepa</s>). He sees the <s>Buddha</s>-fields as having the characteristic of space; what is accomplished, he sees as peaceful <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is <s>mati</s>.

body.text: iti bositvaścarandhyānamṛddhi prajñāmupāyaṃ mati ca vibhajya caturvastūnyācaratyavāptotyanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim | bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhyānamācarannopalabhate 'kuśalacittamakṣomyadharmatayā paripūrayati dhyānapāramitām ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, practicing <s>dhyāna</s>, dividing <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and <s>mati</s> (insight) into four categories, practices these and attains the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, practicing <s>dhyāna</s>, does not perceive an unwholesome mind; through the nature of imperturbability (<s>akṣomyadharmatā</s>), he fulfills the perfection of meditation (<s>dhyānapāramitā</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre dhyānapāramitā nāmāṣṭamo vargaḥ |)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the eighth chapter, called 'The Perfection of Meditation (<s>Dhyānapāramitā</s>),' [is concluded].)

body.text: navami vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Ninth Chapter

body.text: prajñāpāramitā
body.translated_text: The Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvaḥ kathaṃ bhāvayati prajñām | prajñā hyātmaparābhayalābhāyacedevaṃvidhā prajñā niṣpādayati bodhimārgam | bodhisattvaḥ kāmayate vinetuṃ sattvānaparhatuṃ duḥkhāni bhāvayati tasmātprajñām | bhāvayanprajñāṃ śikṣate sarvalokadhātuvastūni | prajahāti lobhadvepamohān pratiṣṭhāpayati mahāmaitrīm | karuṇāyamāna upakaroti sattvān | nityaṃ paritrātumicchaṃsteṣāṃ pariṇāyako bhavati | vibhajya deśayati sadasanmārgaṃ kuśalākuśalāśca vipākāniti bodhisattvasyādiprajñācittam ||
body.translated_text: 1. How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivate wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>)? If wisdom is for the benefit of self, others, and both — such wisdom accomplishes the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>). The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, desiring to discipline beings and remove sufferings, cultivates wisdom for that reason. Cultivating wisdom, he studies all the matters of all world-realms (<s>lokadhātu</s>). He abandons greed (<s>lobha</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>), and establishes great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>). Practicing compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), he benefits beings. Always wishing to protect them, he becomes their leader. He distinguishes and teaches the right and wrong paths, and the wholesome and unwholesome fruits (<s>vipāka</s>) — this is the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s initial wisdom-mind.

body.text: 2 || prajñābhāvanāhetoḥ prajahātyavidyām | apākurute kleśāvaraṇaṃ jñeyāvaraṇamityasyātmalābhaḥ | vinayansattvānparisāntvayatīti paralābha| carittvānuttarāṃ bodhiṃ sattveṣu pariṇāmyātmanā salābhinaḥ karotītyubhayalābhaḥ | prajñābhāvanayā prāpnoti prathamāṃ bhūmi yāvatsarvajñatāmiti niṣpādayati bodhimārgam ||
body.translated_text: 2. Through the cause of cultivating wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), one abandons ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), removes the obstruction of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the obstruction of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) — this is one's own benefit (<s>ātmalābha</s>). Disciplining and consoling beings — this is the benefit of others (<s>paralābha</s>). Having practiced the unsurpassed awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) and dedicating it to beings, one makes oneself and others beneficiaries — this is the benefit of both (<s>ubhayalābha</s>). Through the cultivation of wisdom, one attains the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>) up to omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) — thus one accomplishes the path of awakening (<s>bodhimārga</s>).

body.text: 3 | prajñāṃ bhāvayanbodhisattvaḥkrameṇa pratiṣṭhāpayati viśati cittāni | kāni viśatiḥ | (1) kuśalakāmānutpādayato 'sya kalyāṇamitrānutsargacittam | (2) madamānaṃ parityajato 'syāpramādacittam | (3) anucarataḥ sikṣāpadāni prītaṃ dharmaśravaṇacittam | (4) dharmāñchṛṇvato 'viśrāntaṃ kuśalacintācittam | (5) bhāvayataścaturi brahmavihārānsamyagjñānacittam | (6) paśyato 'śūcicaryāṃ tataḥ śrāmyataḥ parityāgacittam | (7) paśyata āryasatyāni poḍaśākāraṃ cittam | (8) paśyato dvādaśāṅgapratītyasamutpādaṃ bhāvayataḥ prajñācittam | (9) śṛṇvataḥ pāramitāḥ tatsaṃgrahakāmacittam | (10) anityaduḥkhānātmatāṃ paśyataḥ śāntaṃ nirvāṇaṃ cittam | (11) paśyataḥ śūnyamalakṣaṇamapraṇihitaṃ niṣkriyacittam | (12) paśyataḥ skandhadhātvāyatanāni bhūya ādīnavacittam (13)kleśāñjayato 'sahacaracittam | (14) pālayataḥ kuśaladharmānātmasahacaracitam | (15) nivārayato 'kuśaladharmānprahāṇacittam | (16) ācarataḥ samyagdharmaṃ vipulacittam | (17) ācarato yānadvayamapi nityamupekṣācittam | (18) śṛṇvanbodhisattvapiṭakaṃ pramodānusaraṇacittam | (19) svalābhaparalābhāvanusaṃvardhayataḥ sarvakuśalakarmacittam | (20) gṛhṇataḥ sucaritaṃ sarvabuddhadharmagaveṣaṇācittam ||
body.translated_text: 3. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivating wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) progressively establishes and enters [twenty] minds. What are the twenty? (1) From generating wholesome desires — the mind of not abandoning spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>). (2) From abandoning pride and arrogance (<s>madamāna</s>) — the mind of non-heedlessness (<s>apramāda</s>). (3) From following the training rules (<s>śikṣāpada</s>) — the joyful mind of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. (4) From hearing the <s>Dharma</s> — the unceasing mind of wholesome contemplation. (5) From cultivating the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) — the mind of right knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>). (6) From seeing impure conduct and becoming wearied thereby — the mind of renunciation (<s>parityāga</s>). (7) From seeing the Noble Truths (<s>āryasatya</s>) — the mind of the sixteen aspects. (8) From seeing the twelve-linked dependent origination (<s>dvādaśāṅgapratītyasamutpāda</s>) and cultivating it — the mind of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). (9) From hearing the perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>) — the mind desiring to gather them. (10) From seeing impermanence, suffering, and non-self (<s>anityaduḥkhānātmatā</s>) — the peaceful <s>nirvāṇa</s>-mind. (11) From seeing emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>), signlessness (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>), and wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>) — the mind of non-activity (<s>niṣkriya</s>). (12) From seeing the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) — the mind [seeing] ever greater danger. (13) From conquering the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) — the mind of non-companionship [with them]. (14) From guarding wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — the mind of self-companionship. (15) From preventing unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — the mind of abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>). (16) From practicing the right <s>Dharma</s> — the expansive mind (<s>vipulacitta</s>). (17) From practicing the two vehicles as well — always the mind of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). (18) From hearing the <s>Bodhisattvapiṭaka</s> — the mind of joyful following. (19) From increasing one's own and others' gain — the mind of all wholesome actions. (20) From taking up good conduct — the mind seeking all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>.

body.text: 4 | punaḥkhalu prajñāṃ bhavayato bodhisattvasya bhavanti daśadharmāḥ kuśalacintācittāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhāveṇikāḥ | ke daśa | (1)vibhajya cintayati samādhiprajñāmūlam | (2)cintayanna parityajati śāśvatocchedāntadvayam | (3) cintayati pratītyasamutpādadharmān | (4) cintayati na sattvo nātmā na pudgalo na jīva iti | (5) cintayati na santi triṣvadhsvātītānāgatapratyutpannadharmāḥ | (6) cintayatyanutpannamapi karma nocchinatti hetuphalam | (7) cintayam dharmān śūnyanapya kusīdaścāvaropayati kuśalam | (8) cintayatyalakṣaṇaṃ na ca pratinivartate nirvāpayituṃ sattvān | (9) cintayannapyapraṇihitaṃ na jahāti gaveṣayituṃ bodhim | (10) cintayannapyakṛtaṃ na pariharati prakāśayituṃ sāṃbhogikaṃ kāyam ||
body.translated_text: 4. Furthermore, for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> cultivating wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), there are ten <s>dharmas</s> of wholesome contemplation-mind that are not shared with <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. What are the ten? (1) Analyzing, one contemplates the root of concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). (2) Contemplating, one does not abandon the two extremes of eternalism and annihilationism (<s>śāśvatocchedānta</s>). (3) One contemplates the <s>dharmas</s> of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). (4) One contemplates: 'There is no being (<s>sattva</s>), no self (<s>ātman</s>), no person (<s>pudgala</s>), no life-force (<s>jīva</s>).' (5) One contemplates that there are no <s>dharmas</s> in the three times — past, future, and present. (6) One contemplates that even though <s>karma</s> is unborn, it does not cut off cause and effect (<s>hetupahala</s>). (7) Contemplating <s>dharmas</s> as empty, yet without being lazy, one plants wholesome [seeds]. (8) Contemplating signlessness (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>), yet one does not turn back from extinguishing [the suffering of] beings. (9) Contemplating wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), yet one does not abandon the search for awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). (10) Contemplating the uncreated (<s>akṛta</s>), yet one does not give up manifesting the enjoyment body (<s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s>).

body.text: 5 | punaḥ khalu bodhisattvasya dvādaśa bhavanti kuśalāvatāradharmamukhāni (1) śūnyatādisamādhiṣvavatārakuśalo 'pi na (tān) gṛhṇāti | (2) dhyānasamādhiṣvavatārakuśalo 'pi na yathādhyānaṃ tatropapadyate | (3) ṛddhijñāneṣvavatārakuśalo 'pi nānāsravān dharmān labhate | (4) adhyātmaparyavekṣaṇadharmeṣvavatārakuśalo 'pi na teṣu niścayamanuprāpnoti | (5) sarvasattvaśūnyatādṭaṣṭāvavatārakuśalo 'pi nopekṣate mahāmaitrīm | (6) sarvasattvānātmatādṭaṣṭavavatārakuśalo 'pi nopekṣate mahākaruṇām | (7) durgayupapattāvatārakuśalo 'pi na sa karmanimittaṃ tatropapadyate| (8) vairāgyāvatārakuśalo 'pi na vairāgyadharmān pratilabhate | (9) kāmasukhaparityāgāvatārakuśalo 'pi nopekṣate dharmasukham | (10) prapaṃcamatavādaparityāgāvatārakuśalo 'pi nopekṣate upāyadṭaṣṭīḥ | (11) bahvādīnavāḥ saṃskṛta dharmā ityanucintanāvatārakuśalo 'pi nopekṣate saṃskṛtam | (12) paramapariśuddheṣvasaṃskṛtadharmeṣvavatārakuśalo 'pināsaṃskṛte pratiṣṭhito bhavati | bodhisattvaścetsarvakuśalāvatāradharmamukhānyācarati samyagjānāti śūnyatāṃ triṣvadhvasu ba kiciditi ||
body.translated_text: 5. Furthermore, for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> there are twelve doors of skillful entry into wholesome <s>dharmas</s> (<s>kuśalāvatāradharmamukhāni</s>). (1) Though skillful in entering <s>samādhis</s> of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and the rest, one does not grasp them. (2) Though skillful in entering <s>dhyāna</s>-<s>samādhis</s>, one does not take rebirth in those [realms] according to the <s>dhyāna</s>. (3) Though skillful in supernatural knowledge (<s>ṛddhijñāna</s>), one does not [thereby] attain the outflow-free <s>dharmas</s>. (4) Though skillful in <s>dharmas</s> of inner contemplation (<s>adhyātmaparyavekṣaṇa</s>), one does not reach certainty in them. (5) Though skillful in the view of emptiness of all beings, one does not abandon great loving-kindness (<s>mahāmaitrī</s>). (6) Though skillful in the view of non-self (<s>anātmatā</s>) of all beings, one does not abandon great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). (7) Though skillful in entering the lower destinies [for beings' sake], one does not take birth there due to <s>karma</s>. (8) Though skillful in dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), one does not [fully] attain the <s>dharmas</s> of dispassion. (9) Though skillful in abandoning sensual pleasures (<s>kāmasukha</s>), one does not abandon the joy of <s>Dharma</s>. (10) Though skillful in abandoning proliferation and doctrinal disputation (<s>prapañcamatavāda</s>), one does not abandon skillful views (<s>upāyadṛṣṭi</s>). (11) Though skillful in contemplating that conditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) have many dangers, one does not abandon the conditioned. (12) Though skillful in entering the supremely pure unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), one does not remain fixed in the unconditioned. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> practices all these doors of skillful entry into wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, he rightly knows emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) in the three times — that there is nothing whatsoever [to grasp].

body.text:
6 | yadi caivaṃ paśyati paśyati triṣvadhvasu śūnyatāṃ prajñābalahetoḥ | yadi cāvaropitāni triṣvadhvasu tathāgatairaprameyāṇi puṇyānyakhilaṃ pariṇāmayatyanuttarāyāṃ bodhau tadevaṃ bodhisattvaḥ saṃpaśyati triṣvadhvasūpāyam|
punarapi paśyannatītāndharmānkṣapitānanāgatānnāgatānsadaivācaratikuśalaṃ parākramate na ca kusado bhavati | anutpannānapi paśyannagatāndharmānparākramate kāmayate bodhim | kṣaṇaṃ kṣaṇaṃ nirudhyamānānpaśyannapi pratyutyannāndharmān bodhimupagantuṃ na cāsya cittavismṛtirityevaṃ bodhisattvaḥ paśyati triṣvadhvasūpāyam |
niruddhamatītaṃ nāgatamanāgatamasthiraṃ pratyutpannam | api ca paśyandharmāñcittacaittānutpadyamānānnirudhyamānānviśīryamāṇānpūyamānānnopekṣate saṃgrahītuṃkuśalamūlāni | upacarati bodhidharmānityevaṃ bodhisattvaḥ paśyati triṣvadhvasūpāmam |
body.translated_text: 6. If one thus sees — one sees emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) in the three times through the power of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). If the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have planted immeasurable merits in the three times and dedicate them entirely to the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s>, then thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) in the three times. Furthermore, seeing that past <s>dharmas</s> are exhausted and future ones have not yet come, one always practices the wholesome, exerts effort, and does not become lazy. Seeing that future <s>dharmas</s> are unarisen, one exerts effort and desires <s>bodhi</s>. Seeing that present <s>dharmas</s> are ceasing moment by moment, one does not forget the mind [intent on] approaching <s>bodhi</s> — thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees skillful means in the three times. The past has ceased; the future has not come; the present is unstable. Moreover, seeing <s>dharmas</s> — mind and mental factors — arising, ceasing, disintegrating, and decaying, one does not neglect to accumulate roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). One engages with the <s>dharmas</s> of awakening — thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees skillful means in the three times.

body.text:
7 | punaḥ khalu bodhisattvaḥ paśyati sarvaṃ kuśalamakuśalamātmānamanātmānaṃ bhūtamabhūtaṃ śūnyamaśūnyaṃ saṃvṛtaṃ paramārthaṃ samyaksamādhi mithyāsamādhi saṃskṛtamasaṃskṛtaṃ sāsravamanāsravaṃ kṛṣṇadharmaṃ śukladharmaṃ jātimaraṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ dharmadhātusvabhāvamekalakṣaṇamalakṣaṇam | na ca tatra dharmā ityucyate 'lakṣaṇamiti | api nāma kaścana dharmo yohyalakṣaṇo nāmetyucyate sarvadharmamudrākṣayāmudrā | āsu mudrāsu na mudrālakṣaṇamityucyate satyaṃ bhūtaṃ prajñopāyaḥ prajñāpāramitā |
utpāditabādhicettena bodhisattvenaivaṃ śikṣiotavyamevaṃ bhāvayitavyam | evaṃ bhāvayannavāpnotyanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim | bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prajñāṃ bhāvayato na cittaṃ carati dharmatāyāḥ pariśuddhatvāt | evaṃ paripūrayati prajñāpāramitām ||
body.translated_text: 7. Furthermore, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> sees everything: wholesome and unwholesome, self and non-self, real and unreal, empty and non-empty, conventional (<s>saṃvṛta</s>) and ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>), right <s>samādhi</s> and wrong <s>samādhi</s>, conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) and without outflows (<s>anāsrava</s>), dark <s>dharmas</s> and white <s>dharmas</s>, birth-and-death and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the own-nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), single-characteristic and characteristicless. Regarding those, it is said 'characteristicless' — not '<s>dharmas</s>.' If there is indeed any <s>dharma</s> that is called 'characteristicless,' that is the seal of all <s>dharmas</s> — the seal of inexhaustibility (<s>akṣayamudrā</s>). In these seals, 'there is no characteristic of a seal' — this is said to be true, real, the skillful means of <s>prajñā</s>, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has generated <s>bodhicitta</s> should thus train and thus cultivate. Cultivating thus, one attains the unsurpassed perfect awakening. For the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> cultivating <s>prajñā</s>, the mind does not move [in objects] — because of the purity of <s>dharmatā</s> (reality-nature). Thus one fulfills the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre prajñāpāramitā nāma navamo vargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the ninth chapter, called 'The Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>),' [is concluded].)

body.text: daśamo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Tenth Chapter

body.text: tathātādharmamukhaṃ
body.translated_text: The Gateway of the <s>Dharma</s> of Suchness (<s>Tathatādharmamukha</s>)

body.text: 1 | kulaputreṇa kuladuhitrā vā caratā ṣaṭ pāramitā gaveṣayatānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ prahātavyāḥ sapta dharmāḥ | katame sapta | prathamaṃ prajahātyakalpāṇamitrāṇi | akalyāṇamitrāṇi śikṣayanti parihartamanuttarāṃ śraddhāmudāttaṃ saṃkalpamanuttamaṃ vīryaṃ samuccetuṃ ca saṃkliṣṭācārān | dvitīyaṃ prajahāti strīrūpaṃ kāmarāgaṃ pṛthagjanairvivikto bhavatyasahacaraḥ | tṛtīyaṃ paśyannātmānamābhāsaṃ prajahātyasadgrāhaṃ snehabahumānānurāgāṃściraṃ sthāsyatīti | caturthaṃ prajahāti dveṣapratidhamauddhatyaṃ mānamīrṣvāmasūyāṃ yato jayate kalahaḥ pratihanyate kuśalacittam | pañcamaṃ prajahāti pramādaṃ madamānaṃ kausīdyaṃ svakaṃ parittakuśalaṃ ca yenāvajānāti parān | ṣaṣṭhaṃ prajahāti tairthikāgamaṃ kāvyāni na cābuddhabhāṣitāni praśaṃsati | saptamaṃ nopagacchati mithyādṭaṣṭimasamyagdṭaṣṭim | evamime saptadharmāḥ prahātavyāḥ | uktaṃ bhagavatā na paśyāmi tathānyāndharmānya āvṛṇvanti buddhamārgaṃ yatheme saptadharmāḥ| ataeva bodhisattvena prahātavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 1. A son or daughter of good family who practices the six perfections (<s>ṣaṭpāramitā</s>) and seeks the unsurpassed perfect awakening should abandon seven <s>dharmas</s>. What are the seven? First, one abandons unwholesome friends (<s>akalyāṇamitra</s>) — unwholesome friends who teach [one] to discard the unsurpassed faith, the noble resolve, the supreme vigor, and to accumulate defiled conduct. Second, one abandons attachment to feminine form and sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>), living apart from ordinary beings, without companions. Third, seeing oneself as a mere appearance (<s>ābhāsa</s>), one abandons the wrong grasping and the attachments of affection, esteem, and passion [thinking] 'it will last long.' Fourth, one abandons hatred, retaliation, agitation, pride, envy, and jealousy — from which arise quarrel and the destruction of the wholesome mind. Fifth, one abandons heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>), intoxication, pride, laziness, and one's own limited wholesomeness by which one looks down on others. Sixth, one abandons the scriptures of <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) and poetry, and does not praise what was not spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>. Seventh, one does not approach wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) and incorrect views. Thus these seven <s>dharmas</s> should be abandoned. The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'I do not see any other <s>dharmas</s> that obstruct the <s>Buddha</s>-path as do these seven <s>dharmas</s>.' Therefore the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should abandon them.

body.text: 2 | aciramanuttarāṃ sambodhimabhisamboddhukāmenācaritavyāḥ saptadharmāḥ | ke sapta | prathamaṃbodhisattvenopagantavyāni kalpāṇa mitrāṇi | kalpāṇamitrāṇi buddhā bodhisattvāśca | śrāvakā api bodhisattvaṃ gambhīradharmakośe pāramitāsu saṃpratiṣṭhāpayanto bhavanti bodhisattvasya kalpāṇamitrāṇi | dvitīyaṃ bodhisattvenopacaritavyāḥ pravrajitā āraṇyakadharmāśca | mātṛgrāmaḥ prahātavyaḥ kāmarāgaśca | viviktena bhavitavyaṃ pṛthagjanairasahacareṇa | tṛtīyaṃ bodhisattvena draṣṭavyaḥ kāyo malabhūmivadaśucisaṃśrayaḥ kevalaṃ vātaśleṣmapittalohitakamarāgārho dine dine maraṇonmukho 'nādarabuddhyā parihartavyaḥ sotsāhaṃ bhāvayitavyo mārgaḥ | caturthaṃ bodhisattvena nityaṃ caritavyā śāntiḥ kṣāntirgurukaraṇīyā mṛdutāca | śikṣayitavyāḥ kṣāntau sthāpayitavyāśca janāḥ | paṃcamaṃ bodhisattvenācaritavyaṃ vīryamutpādayitavyā hrīrapatrapā ca pūjayitavya upādhyāyaḥ karuṇāyitavyā dīnā duḥkhitāndṭaṣṭrā svakāyena parigrahītavyaṃ tadduḥkham | ṣaṣṭhaṃ bodhisattvenabhāvayitavyaṃ vipulaṃ mahāyānabodhisattvapiṭakaṃ grahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā dharmmā buddhānuśaṃsitāḥ | saptamaṃ bodhisattvenopagantavyaṃ bhāvayitavyaṃ paramārthasatyam | tathāhi | bhūtalakṣaṇamekalakṣaṇamalakṣaṇam bodhisattvaścetkāmayate śīghramabhisambodhimabhyupagantavyā evamime sapta dharmāḥ |
body.translated_text: 2. Seven <s>dharmas</s> must be practiced by one who desires to quickly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā saṃbodhi</s>). What are the seven? First, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should approach virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitrāṇi</s>). The virtuous friends are <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Even <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) who establish the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in the deep treasury of <s>Dharma</s> and in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) are the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s virtuous friends. Second, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should undertake the going-forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and the forest-dwelling practices (<s>āraṇyakadharma</s>). Women (<s>mātṛgrāma</s>) and sensual desire (<s>kāmarāga</s>) should be abandoned. One should dwell in seclusion, without the companionship of ordinary people (<s>pṛthagjana</s>). Third, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should see the body as a receptacle of impurity like a ground of filth, consisting merely of wind, phlegm, bile, and blood, a base of desire — facing death day by day, it should be relinquished with a mind of non-attachment; with enthusiasm the path should be cultivated. Fourth, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should always practice tranquility (<s>śānti</s>), make patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) paramount and gentleness too. People should be trained and established in patience. Fifth, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should practice vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), generate moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and modesty (<s>apatrāpya</s>), honor the preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), feel compassion for the poor, suffering, and afflicted, and take on their suffering with one's own body. Sixth, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should cultivate the vast <s>Mahāyāna Bodhisattva Piṭaka</s>; one should grasp, retain, and recite the <s>dharmas</s> praised by the <s>Buddhas</s>. Seventh, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> should approach and cultivate the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). For thus: the characteristic of reality is the one characteristic, which is no characteristic. If the <s>Bodhisattva</s> desires to quickly fully awaken, these seven <s>dharmas</s> should be practiced.

body.text: 3 | punaḥ khalu puruṣaḥ prāptihetorutpādayati ced bodhicittamaprameyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ kalpaṃ saṃgṛhṇati maitrīṃkaruṇāṃ muditāmupekṣāṃ dānaṃ śīlaṃ kṣāntiṃ vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñām | jñātavyaṃ na sa puruṣaḥ prajñahāti jātimaraṇam | na ca gacchati bodhim | tatkasya hetoḥ | [bodhi-]cittaprāptirapyasti prāptidṭaṣṭiḥ skandhadhātvāyatanadṭaṣṭirātmadṭaṣṭiḥ pudgaladṭasṭiḥ sattvadṭaṣṭi jīrvadṭaṣṭi maitrīkaruṇāmuditopokṣādānaśīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñādidṭaṣṭiḥ | saṃkṣepata ucyate | buddhadharmasaṃghadṭaṣṭirnirvāṇadṭaṣṭirevaṃ yatkiñcatprāptavyadṭaṣṭiḥ sarvameṣa āsaṅga | cittāsaṃga evocyate mithyādṭaṣṭiḥ | kasmāt | puruṣā mithyādṭaṣṭayaścakavatparivartante trighātau sadaiva parihīyante vimukteḥ | ayamepa āsaṃgaḥ | na caivaṃ kadāpi nirmucyate| na cāpnuvantyayanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 3. Furthermore, if a person, for the sake of attainment, generates <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) and for immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) gathers <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — it should be known that such a person does not go beyond birth and death, nor does he reach <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). For what reason? Because there is still the view of attainment (<s>prāptidṛṣṭi</s>) regarding the attainment of <s>bodhicitta</s> — the view of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), the view of a person (<s>pudgaladṛṣṭi</s>), the view of a being (<s>sattvadṛṣṭi</s>), the view of a life-force (<s>jīvadṛṣṭi</s>), and the views regarding <s>maitrī</s>, <s>karuṇā</s>, <s>muditā</s>, <s>upekṣā</s>, <s>dāna</s>, <s>śīla</s>, <s>kṣānti</s>, <s>vīrya</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>prajñā</s>, and so forth. Stated briefly: the view of <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>; the view of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — thus, whatever view of something to be attained — all of this is attachment (<s>āsaṅga</s>). The attachment of mind is itself called wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>). Why? People with wrong views revolve like a wheel in the three unfortunate destinies (<s>durgati</s>) and are always deprived of liberation (<s>vimukti</s>). This is that very attachment. Thus one is never liberated, nor does one attain the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: 4 | puruṣaścedutpādayati bodhicittaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ cittaṃ śūnyalakṣaṇam | kicittaṃ kathaṃ ca śūnyalakṣaṇam | cittaṃ nāma manovijñānamevaṃ vijñānaskandho mana āyatanaṃ mano dhātuḥ | cittaṃ śūnyalakṣaṇaṃ na cittaṃ cittalakṣaṇaṃ na ca kartṛ| kasmāt | yā cittalakṣaṇaśūnyatā sā na ca kartrī na ca kārayitrī | yadi kaścitkarttaiva nāsti na tarhi kartṛlakṣaṇam | yadi bodhisattvo jānātyevaṃ dharmānsarvadharmeṣvanāsakto bhavati | anāsaktiheto rna jānātikuśalākuśalaphalavipāka iti ācaritāyāṃ maintryāṃ jānāti nāstyātmā | acaritāyāṃ karuṇāyāṃ na sattvāḥ | ācaritāyāṃ muditāyāṃ na jīvaḥ | ācaritāyāmupekṣāyāṃ na pudgalaḥ | ācarannapi dānaṃ na paśyati dānavastu | ācarannapi śīlaṃ na paśyati cittaviśuddhim | ācarannapi kṣāntiṃ na paśyati sattvān | ācarannapi vīryaṃ na jahāti rāgacitam | ācarannapi dhyānaṃ parityajati nākuśalacittam | bhāvayato 'pi prajñāṃ na ca kācicittabhāvanā | sarvalaṃbanā sarvaprajñā na cāsaṅgo 'sya prajñāyām | na ca prajñāvāptirna ca prajñā dṭaṣṭiḥ | ya ācaratyevamācarati prajñāṃ | na catasyācaritaṃ bhavati kiṃcita na cāpi nācaritaṃ bhavati kiṃcit | antaḥ pariśuddho 'pi sa vinetuṃ sattvanācarati ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ | ya acaratyevaṃ bhāvayati cittaṃ kṣaṇamavaropitakuśalasyāpi tasya puṇyaphalavipāko 'prameyo 'paryantaḥ | asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpakoṭiśatasahasrairapi na tasyāntaḥ | avāpnoti so 'nāyāsenānuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 4. If a person generates <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening), one should see that the mind has the mark of emptiness (<s>śūnyalakṣaṇa</s>). What is mind, and how does it have the mark of emptiness? Mind is <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness); thus it is the consciousness aggregate (<s>vijñānaskandha</s>), the mind sense-base (<s>mana āyatana</s>), the mind element (<s>manodhātu</s>). Mind has the mark of emptiness — mind is not the mark of mind, nor is it an agent. Why? That which is the emptiness of the mark of mind is neither an agent nor a cause of action. If indeed there is no agent whatsoever, then there is no mark of an agent. If a <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) thus, one becomes unattached to all <s>dharmas</s>. Through the cause of non-attachment, one does not know the ripening of wholesome and unwholesome fruits. In the practice of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), one knows: 'there is no self.' In the practice of <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion): 'there are no beings.' In the practice of <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy): 'there is no life-force.' In the practice of <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity): 'there is no person.' Even while practicing <s>dāna</s> (giving), one does not see the object of giving. Even while practicing <s>śīla</s> (morality), one does not see the purification of mind. Even while practicing <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), one does not see beings. Even while practicing <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), one does not abandon the passionate mind. Even while practicing <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), one does not relinquish the unwholesome mind. Even while cultivating <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), there is no cultivation of mind whatsoever. All supports, all wisdom — yet there is no attachment to wisdom. There is no attainment of wisdom, and wisdom is not a view. One who practices thus practices <s>prajñā</s>. There is nothing that has been practiced, and there is nothing that has not been practiced. Though inwardly purified, in order to discipline beings one practices the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections). One who practices thus and cultivates the mind — even for one who has planted wholesome [seeds] for [merely] a moment, the ripening of the fruit of merit is immeasurable and limitless. Even in innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), there is no end to it. That person attains the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) with ease.

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstretathatādharmamukhaṃ nāma daśamo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the tenth chapter, called 'The <s>Tathatā</s> (Suchness) Dharma-gate.')

body.text: ekadaśo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Eleventh Chapter

body.text: śūnyālakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: The Mark of Emptiness (<s>Śūnyalakṣaṇa</s>)

body.text: 1 | ekasminsamaye bhagavānpurā viharati smaveṇuvane kalandakanivāpe mahatā [bhikṣu]saṃghena sārddhamaprameyeṇa | atha bhagavāndeśayituṃ saddharmamāmantrayati sma mahāsaṃgham | bhagavānavocat| sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥ śūnyā niḥsārā aśraddheyāḥ sarvalokaiḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ | rūpaṃ na bandho na mokṣaḥ | vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāvijñānaṃ na bandho na mokṣaḥ | rūpalakṣaṇaṃ tyajati ca lakṣaṇam vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānanyalakṣaṇāni tyajanti ca kṣaṇāni | cakṣūrūpaśrotraśabdaghrāṇagandhajihvārasakāyaspraṣṭavyamanodharmā apyevam | na te grāhyā nopekṣyā na samalā na vimalā jagatā nānugatā na pratigatā nābhākharā na bhākharā na moho na prajñā na caipo 'nto na so 'nta nāpi ca madhyasrota iticocyate na bandhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 1. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was formerly dwelling in the Bamboo Grove (<s>Veṇuvana</s>), at the Squirrel Feeding Place (<s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>), together with a great and immeasurable assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks). Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wishing to teach the true <s>Dharma</s>, addressed the great assembly. The <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke: 'All <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are without own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), empty, without essence, and unbelievable to all worldly beings. For what reason? Form (<s>rūpa</s>) is neither bondage nor liberation. Feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) are neither bondage nor liberation. The mark of form abandons [its own] mark; the marks of feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness abandon [their own] marks in an instant. The eye and form, ear and sound, nose and smell, tongue and taste, body and tangible objects, mind and <s>dharmas</s> — likewise. They are not to be grasped nor to be disregarded; they are neither impure nor pure; they do not follow the world nor go against it; they are neither without syllables nor with syllables; they are neither delusion nor wisdom; there is no end here nor end there, nor even a middle stream — thus it is said: there is no bondage.'

body.text: 2 | bandhābhāvācchūnyam | śūnyamucyate 'lakṣaṇam | alakṣaṇamapi śūnyamityucyate śūnyam | śūnyamucyate 'kṣaṇamakṣaṇamapi śūnyamityucyate śūnyam | śūnyakṣaṇamapi śūnyamityuccate śūnyam | śūnyatāyāṃna kuśakaṃ na cā kuśalaṃ na cāpi śūnyalakṣaṇamityucyate śūnyam | bodhisattvo yadyevaṃ jānāti skandhadhātvāyatanasvabhāvaṃ na cagṛhṇātītyucyate dharmakṣāntiḥ | bodhisattva evaṃvidhakṣāntihetoḥ prāpnot vyākaraṇakṣāntim ||
body.translated_text: 2. Because bondage does not exist, [all is] empty. The empty is called 'without marks' (<s>alakṣaṇa</s>). That which is without marks is also called empty — empty. The empty is called 'without moments' (<s>akṣaṇa</s>); that which is without moments is also called empty — empty. That which is the empty moment is also called empty — empty. In emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) there is neither the wholesome nor the unwholesome, nor even the mark of emptiness — thus it is called empty. When a <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows thus the own-nature of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) and does not grasp [them], this is called <s>dharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of dharmas). Through the cause of such patience, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains <s>vyākaraṇakṣānti</s> (the patient acceptance that leads to prophecy).

body.text: 3 | buddhaputrāstathāhi bodhisattvo likhatyākāśe tathāgatasya dvādaśaṅḥapravacanāni | atīteṣvaprameyeṣu kalpeṣu parinirvṛteṣu buddhadharmeṣu puruṣo dharmaṃ gaveṣayanna kicidapi paśyati na ca śṛṇoti sattvā viparivartante kurvanto 'prameyāṇyakuśalāni | punaranyataḥ pariśuddhaprajñajanāḥ karuṇāyante satveṣu gaveṣayanti buddhadharmāngatvā paśyantyākāśe likhitāni lekhaspaṣṭatayāvagacchanti vācayanti gṛhnanti dhārayanti yathābhāṣitamācaranti vibhajya prakāśayantyupakurvanti sattvān | yaśca likhatyākāśe yaśca jānātyākāśākṣarāṇi sa nu cintayituṃ śakyo yaśca vā prakāśayati deśayatyācarati gṛhṇāti dhārayati nayāte sattvānvimocayati vandham ||
body.translated_text: 3. Sons of the <s>Buddha</s>: thus indeed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> writes in space the twelve sections of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s discourses. In immeasurable past <s>kalpas</s>, when the <s>Buddha-dharma</s> had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, a person seeking the <s>Dharma</s> sees nothing and hears nothing — beings revolve, performing immeasurable unwholesome acts. Then, from elsewhere, people of purified wisdom have compassion for beings, seek the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, go [to the place], see what is written in space, clearly comprehend the writing, recite it, grasp it, retain it, practice as it was spoken, and having analyzed and illuminated [it], benefit beings. He who writes in space, and he who knows the letters of space — can that one be conceived? And he who illuminates, teaches, practices, grasps, retains, leads beings, and liberates from bondage?

body.text: 4 | buddhaputrā uktaṃ bhagavatā | atīte 'dhvani gaveṣayanvodhimārgaṃ mayā labdhāni buddhakoṭitrayastriśadaṣṭānavatibuddhaśatasahasrāṇi | sarveṣāṃ kāle 'hamāsaṃ cakravarta sarve cārāgitāstepūjitāste buddhāśca buddhaputrāśca prāptavyahetorna ca mayā prāptaṃ vyākaraṇam | punarlabdhāni pratyekabuddhakoṭicaturaśītiśatasahasrāṇi pratyekabuddhanavatiśatasahasrāṇi ca | sava'pi caturbhiḥ pariṣkārai ryāvajjīvaṃ pūjitāḥ | punaḥ khalu labdhāni dvāpaṣṭibuddhaśatasahasrāṇi ekaṣapṭayuttaradvādaśabuddhaśatāni ca | sarveṣāṃ kāle 'hamāsaṃ cakavartī | ārāgitāścate yāvajjivaṃ pūjitāśca te | parinirvṛteṣu teṣu kāritāḥ saptaratnamayāḥ stūpā dhṛtapūjita [buddha]śarīrāḥ | atha punarlokamāgatā buddhā āmantritā mayādhyepitāḥ prāvartayandharmacakram | pūjitāścaivaṃ buddhānāṃ śatāni sahasrāṇi śatasahasrāṇi śatasahasrāṇi koṭayaśca | te ca tathāgatāḥ śūnyadharmeṣu dharmalakṣaṇamavocan | prāptavyaheto rna mayā prāptaṃ vyākaraṇam ||
body.translated_text: 4. Sons of the <s>Buddha</s>: the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: 'Seeking the <s>bodhi</s>-path in the past, I encountered three trillion and thirty-eight billion nine hundred million <s>Buddhas</s>. At the time of all of them, I was a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch); all were pleased and worshipped — both the <s>Buddhas</s> and the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>. Yet the cause for attainment had not come — I did not receive a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). Again, I encountered eighty-four trillion and ninety billion <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. All were worshipped with the four requisites for as long as they lived. Again, I encountered sixty-two billion and twelve hundred and sixty-one <s>Buddhas</s>. At the time of all of them, I was a <s>cakravartin</s>; they were pleased and worshipped for as long as they lived. When they had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, <s>stūpas</s> made of the seven jewels were erected, and their relics were held and worshipped. Then again, the <s>Buddhas</s> who came into the world were invited and requested by me, and they turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>. Thus hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands, and millions of <s>Buddhas</s> were worshipped. And those <s>Tathāgatas</s> declared the characteristic of <s>dharma</s> regarding the empty <s>dharmas</s> (<s>śūnyadharma</s>). Yet the cause for attainment had not come — I did not receive a prophecy.'

body.text: 5 | evaṃ viparivartamānasya me tāvajjāto dīpaṃkarastathāgataḥ | apaśyaṃ taṃ bhagavantamaśṛṇvaṃ dharmam | labdhā ca sarvānutpādā dharmakṣāntistadā labdhaṃ vyākaraṇam | dīpaṃkareṇa tathāgatena śūnyadharmeṣu bhāṣitaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam | paritrātānyaprameyasattvasahasrāṇi na tathāpi bhāṣitaṃ kiñcinna ca paritrātaḥ kaścit | lokamāgatena lokanāyakamuninā satsvapi śūnyadharmeṣu bhāṣitaṃ lekhitaṃ prakāśitaṃ | lokamāgatena lokanāyakamuninā satsvapi śūnyadharmeṣu bhāṣitaṃ lekhitaṃ prakāśitaṃ śikṣitamāmoditaṃ sarvaśca veditamācaritamapi ca na prakāśitaṃ nāpi veditaṃ na cāpyācaritam | evaṃ dharmāḥ svabhāvalakṣaṇena śūnyāḥ lekhanamapi śūnyam | yo 'bhijānāti so 'pi śūnyaḥ | yo 'bhāṣata so 'pi śūnyaḥ | yaśca janāti so 'pi śūnyaḥ | ādiḥ śūnyamanāgataṃ śūnyaṃ pratyutpannaṃ śūnyam | bodhisattvaḥ saṃgṛhṇandaśa kuśalopāyavalasahasrāṇi sotsāho 'kusīdo puṇyaparipūrito labhate 'nuttarāṃ sanyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 5. 'While thus revolving [in existence], at that time the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> appeared. I saw that <s>Bhagavān</s> and heard the <s>Dharma</s>. And I attained the patience of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpādadharmakṣānti</s>) — then I received the prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>). The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> declared the characteristic of <s>dharma</s> regarding the empty <s>dharmas</s>. Immeasurable thousands of beings were rescued — yet nothing was spoken, and no one was rescued. The world-protector, the sage (<s>muni</s>) who came into the world — even though the empty <s>dharmas</s> exist, he spoke, wrote, and illuminated [them]; he taught, delighted [beings], and everything was made known, practiced — yet nothing was illuminated, nothing was known, nothing was practiced. Thus, <s>dharmas</s> are empty by their own-nature characteristic; writing too is empty; he who comprehends is also empty; he who spoke is also empty; he who knows is also empty. The beginning is empty, the future is empty, the present is empty. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, gathering ten thousand skillful means and powers of the wholesome, zealous and not lazy, fulfilled in merit, attains the unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: 6 | nūnamasukaramacintyaṃ yaducyate dharmābhāve dharmābhāve dharmalakṣaṇaṃ prāptavyābhāve prāptidharmāḥ | buddhagocaramidamevaṃvastvaprameyayaitabuddhaprajñayā kevalaṃ jñātuṃśakyam | na ca jñātuṃ śakyaṃ cintayā | acirotpāditacitto bodhisattvaḥ śraddhācittenānuśaṃsati bodhimārocayati ca | śraddhāhetoḥ krameṇa buddhabhāṣiteṣu viśati | kā nāma śraddhā | śraddhayā paśyati caturāryasatyāni niruṇaddhi kleśān mithyādṭaṣṭisaṃyojanāni | prāpnotyarhatvam | paśyati dvādaśapratyayaṃ dvādaśāṅḥaṃ pratītyasamutpādam | nirudhyante cāsyāvidyājanitāḥ saṃskārā labhate pratyekabuddhatām | śraddhayā carati caturo brahmacihārān ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ prāpnotyanuttārāṃ samyaksambodhimityucyate śraddhākṣāntiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 6. Truly difficult and inconceivable is what is said: in the absence of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>dharma</s>-characteristics [exist]; in the absence of that which is to be attained, the <s>dharmas</s> of attainment [exist]. This is the domain of the <s>Buddha</s> — such a reality can only be known by the immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-wisdom, and cannot be known by thought. A <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has recently generated the mind [of awakening], through the mind of faith (<s>śraddhācitta</s>), follows and illuminates the path of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>). For the sake of faith, one gradually enters into what was spoken by the <s>Buddha</s>. What is this faith?
