Through faith, one sees the four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>), blocks the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and fetters of wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭisaṃyojana</s>), and attains <s>arhatship</s>. One sees the twelve conditions, the twelve-linked dependent origination (<s>dvādaśāṅgapratītyasamutpāda</s>), and the formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) born from ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) are extinguished — one attains <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-hood. Through faith, one practices the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes) and the six perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>), and attains unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) — this is called faith-patience (<s>śraddhākṣānti</s>).

body.text: 7 | sattvā anādimati jātimaraṇalakṣaṇe saktā na paśyanti dharmasvabhāvam | prathamaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ yadepa svakāyaḥ paṃcaskandhaḥ prajñāyate sattva iti | tanna nātmā na sattvaḥ tatkasyahetoḥ tatrātmā cedātmātmavaśas tiṣṭhet | sattvāstu jātiharāvyādhimaraṇaiḥ sadākrāntā nātmavaśās tiṣṭhanti | jñātavyaṃ tena nātmā | anātmatvānna kartā | akartṛtvānnopādātā | dharmasvabhāvaḥ pariśuddhaḥ | nityaṃ tiṣṭhati bhūtakoṭiḥ | evamaparipūritapratyavekṣaṇocyate 'nvayakṣāntiḥ | bodhisattvaścaritvā śraddhākṣānti manvayakṣānti cāciraṃ purayatyanuttarāṃ dharmakṣāntim ||
body.translated_text: 7. Beings, attached to the characteristics of birth and death from beginningless time, do not see the intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmasvabhāva</s>). First, one should see that this very body is cognized as the five aggregates (<s>pañcaskandha</s>) — [what is called] a 'being.' But there is no self (<s>ātman</s>), no being (<s>sattva</s>). Why? Because if there were a self, the self would abide by its own power. But beings, always assailed by birth, aging, disease, and death, do not abide by their own power. Therefore, one should know there is no self. Being without self, there is no agent (<s>kartṛ</s>). Being without agent, there is no appropriator (<s>upādātṛ</s>). The intrinsic nature of <s>dharmas</s> is pure. The limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) always abides. Such incomplete investigation is called consequential patience (<s>anvayakṣānti</s>). Having practiced faith-patience (<s>śraddhākṣānti</s>) and consequential patience (<s>anvayakṣānti</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> quickly fulfills the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-patience (<s>dharmakṣānti</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre śūnyālakṣaṇaṃ nāmaikādaśo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, Emptiness and Signlessness [<s>Śūnyālakṣaṇa</s>], the eleventh chapter.)

body.text: dvādaśo vargaḥ
body.translated_text: Twelfth Chapter

body.text: puṇyaparigrahaḥ
body.translated_text: The Gathering of Merit (<s>Puṇyaparigraha</s>)

body.text: 1 | bodhisattvasyālakṣaṇacittamācaritasyāpi cittaṃ na karmamu pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati | karmalakṣaṇāni jānannapi karoti karmāṇi | kuśalamūlamācarituṃ bodhimamisamboddhuṃ na parityajati saṃskṛtam | satvārthaṃ caranmahākaruṇāṃ nādhitiṣṭhatyasaṃskṛtam | sarvabuddhasamyakprajñārthaṃ na parityajati jātimaraṇaṃ nirvāpayitumaparyantānsattvānanupadhinirvāṇadhātau nādhitiṣṭhati nirvāṇamityucyate bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gambhīraṃ cittamabhisamboddhamanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 1. Even when a <s>Bodhisattva</s> has practiced the signless mind (<s>alakṣaṇacitta</s>), his mind does not become established in [mere] <s>karma</s>. Though knowing the characteristics of <s>karma</s>, one still performs actions. In order to practice wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) and fully awaken to <s>bodhi</s>, one does not abandon the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Acting for the benefit of beings with great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>), one does not remain fixed in the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). For the sake of the right wisdom of all <s>Buddhas</s>, one does not abandon birth and death. In order to extinguish immeasurable beings in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder (<s>anupadhinirvāṇadhātu</s>), one does not remain fixed in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is called the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>'s profound mind for fully awakening to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: 2 | buddhaputrā bodhisattvaḥ paripūrati daśa dharmānna ca pratyāvartate 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksambodheḥ | katame daśa | pathamaṃ bodhisattvo gambhīramutpādayati bodhicittaṃ sattvānapi śikṣayatyutpādayituṃ cittam | dvitīyaṃ nityamabhinandantathāgataṃ priyadānena pūjayati gambhīraṃ cavaropayati kuśalamūlam | tṛtīyaṃ dharmāngaveṣayituṃ gauravacittena pūjayati dharmagurūndharmaḥ śṛṇvanna ca pariśrāgyati | caturthaṃ paśyanbhikṣusaṃghaṃ bhinnaṃ dvidhāvibhaktaṃ paramparaṃ vivadamānaṃ bhaṇḍanaṃ kurvāṇaṃ gavepayatyupāyaṃ saṃgamayati ca | pañcamaṃ paśyannāṣṭre vardhamānānyaśubhāni kṣīyamāṇānbuddhadharmāndeśayati tathā vācayati yāvadekāmapi gāthāṃ yenānucchinno bhavati dharmaḥ | ekacittaṃ paripālayati dharmaṃ na ca gaṇayati kāyajīvitam | ṣaṣṭhaṃ paritrāyate sattvānpaśyanmītānduḥkhitāndadāti cābhayam | saptamaṃ janayati caryotsāhaṃ gaveṣayati caivaṃ mahāyāanaṃ vaipulyamatigambhīraṃ sūtradharmaṃ bodhisattvapiṭakam | aṣṭamaṃ labdhvemāndharmāndhārayati vācayati paryavāpnotiyathābhāṣitamācarati yathābhāṣitamavatiṣṭhate | navamaṃ dharmamadhitiṣṭhannutsāhayati bahutarasattvānpraveṣṭuṃ dharme | daśamaṃ dharme praveśya prakāśayansaṃdarśayaṃllābhaprāmodyavavodhayati sattvān | bodhisattvaḥ paripūryemāndāśadharmānanuttarāyā bodhe rna pratinivartate ||
body.translated_text: 2. O sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> fulfills ten <s>dharmas</s> (qualities) and does not turn back from the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). What are the ten? First, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> generates profound <s>bodhicitta</s> (the mind of awakening) and also trains beings to generate the mind. Second, one always delights in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, worships [him] with offerings of love, and plants profound roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). Third, with a mind of reverence, one worships the teachers of <s>Dharma</s> in order to seek the <s>Dharma</s>; hearing the <s>Dharma</s>, one does not grow weary. Fourth, seeing the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks) split, divided into two, disputing with one another, and quarreling — one seeks skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) and brings them together. Fifth, seeing the unwholesome increasing in the land and the <s>Buddha-dharma</s> declining, one teaches and causes to recite even a single verse, so that the <s>Dharma</s> may not be cut off; one guards the <s>Dharma</s> with a single-pointed mind and does not reckon one's body or life. Sixth, one rescues beings, seeing the terrified and suffering, and gives them fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>). Seventh, one generates enthusiasm for practice and seeks thus the <s>Mahāyāna Vaipulya</s> (extensive), the extremely profound <s>sūtra-dharma</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva-piṭaka</s> (collection of Bodhisattva [teachings]). Eighth, having obtained these <s>dharmas</s>, one retains them, recites them, fully comprehends them, practices as taught, and abides as taught. Ninth, abiding in the <s>Dharma</s>, one encourages an ever greater number of beings to enter into the <s>Dharma</s>. Tenth, having caused [beings] to enter into the <s>Dharma</s>, illuminating and demonstrating it, one causes beings to gain, to rejoice, and to awaken. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who fulfills these ten <s>dharmas</s> does not turn back from the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

body.text: 3 | bodhisattvenācaritavyamevamidaṃsūtram | acintyaṃ khalvevaṃvidhaṃ sūtraṃ yajjanayati sarvamahāmaitrīkaruṇābījam | idaṃ sūtraṃ cittamutpādayituṃ nayati cāvabodhayati ca baddhasattvān | idaṃ sūtramutpādahetu rbodhimabhisaṃprasthitānām | ida sūtraṃ paripūrakaṃ sarvabodhisattvānāmakṣomyacaryāyāḥ | idaṃ sūtramatītānāgatapratyutpannabuddhairanuparigṛhītam | kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraścetkāmayante saṃgrahītumanuttarāṃ bodhi deśayitavyamevaṃ rūpaṃ sūtraṃ | jaṃbūdvīpe 'nucchedāya [buddhadharmāṇāṃ] aprayeyā aparyantāḥ sattvāḥ śṛṇvantvidaṃ sūtram | kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraścecchṛṇvantīdaṃ sūtraṃ labhante 'cintyamatītīkṣṇaṃ mahāprajñāvyūhamaprameyaṃ ca puṇyaphalavipākam | tat kasya hetoḥ | idaṃ sūtraṃ vivṛṇotyaprameyaṃ supariśuddhaṃ prajñānennaṃ karoti buddhavijaṃ nirantaramanucchinnam | paripālayati sattvānaprameyaduḥkhaduḥkhitān | avabhāsayati sarvamavidyāmohāndhakāram | bhinatti caturo mārānmārakarmāṇi ca | nāśāyati sarva tīrthikāṇāṃ mithyādṭaṣṭim | nirvāpayati sarvaṃ kleśamahājvanalam | apanayati [avidyā-]pratyayajanitānsaṃskārān | chinatti lobhaṃ mātsaryaṃ śīlabhedaṃ dveṣaṃ kausīdyaṃ vikṣepaṃ mūḍhatāṃ (ca) ṣaḍ guruvyādhīn | apanayati karmāvaraṇaṃ vipakāvaraṇaṃ kleśāvaraṇaṃ dṭaṣṭyāvaraṇamavidyāvaraṇaṃ jñānāvaraṇaṃbhāvānāvaraṇaṃ | saṃkṣepata ucyate | idaṃ sūtraṃ nirvāpayati niravaśeṣaṃ sarvākuśaladharmān | samedhayati sarvakuśaladharmāgniskandham | kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraścetsūtramidaṃ śrutvārocayantyanumodayantyāścaryacittamutpādayanti jñātavyaṃ taiḥ pūjitā aprameyā buddhāḥ | gambhīramavaropitaṃ kuśalamūlam | tatkasya hetoḥ asya sūtrasya triṣvadhvasu buddhairācaritatvādyaḥ khalu (mārgā-)vacaraḥ śṛṇoti cedaṃ sūtraṃ svātmānaṃ dhanyaṃ manyate | labhate ca mahākuśalalābham | yaḥ kaścillikhatīdaṃ vācayatīdaṃ sūtraṃ jñātavyaṃ sa puruṣaḥ prāpnotyaprameyamaparyantaṃ puṇyaphalavipākam | tatkasya hetoḥ | asya sūtrasyāparyantā lambanatvādapramayamahāpraṇidhānotpādakatvātsarvasattvānugrāhakatvādanuttarasambodhiniṣpādakatvāllabdhaḥ puṇyaphalavipāko 'pyevayameyaḥ | yadi kaścidavabudhyārthaṃ tathācarati yathā sarvabuddhairasaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣvakṣayaprajñayā bhāṣitaṃ tasya puṇyaphalavipāko 'pyakṣayo bhavati | yasminpradeśe dharmaśāstā deśayatīdaṃ sūtraṃ jñātavyaṃ tasminpradeśe stūpaḥ kārayitavyaḥ | kasmāt | samyagdharmasya tatra janitatvāt | edaṃ sūtraṃ yasmindeśe nagarai grāme vihāre kuṭayāṃ vā bhavati jñātavyaṃ tatra bhavati [3 tathāgatasya] dharmakāyaḥ | yadi puruṣaḥ pūjayati gandhapuṣpaiḥ saṃgītena vitānena camaracchatrairgītaiḥ stautrairnamaskāraiḥ jñātavyaṃ sa puruṣa buddhabījaṃ bahulikaroti ki punarvaktavyaṃ yo niravaśeṣaṃ gṛhṇati dhārayati sūtramidam | sa puruṣaḥ pūrayati puṇyaprajñāniṣpattimanāgate 'dhvani labhate vyākaraṇaṃ prāpnityanuttarāṃ samyaksambodhim ||
body.translated_text: 3. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should practice this <s>sūtra</s> thus. Inconceivable indeed is such a <s>sūtra</s>, which generates the seed of all great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion). This <s>sūtra</s> leads [beings] to generate the mind [of awakening] and also awakens bound beings. This <s>sūtra</s> is the cause of arising for those who have set forth toward <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). This <s>sūtra</s> is the fulfiller of the immovable conduct (<s>akṣobhyacaryā</s>) of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. This <s>sūtra</s> is embraced by the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. Sons and daughters of good family, if they desire to gather the unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s>, should teach a <s>sūtra</s> of such form. In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, for the non-interruption [of the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>], immeasurable, limitless beings hear this <s>sūtra</s>. Sons and daughters of good family who hear this <s>sūtra</s> obtain the inconceivable, exceedingly sharp array of great wisdom (<s>mahāprajñāvyūha</s>) and immeasurable ripening of the fruit of merit. For what reason? This <s>sūtra</s> reveals the immeasurable, supremely pure wisdom; through wisdom it makes the <s>Buddha</s>-seed continuous and uninterrupted. It protects beings afflicted by immeasurable suffering. It illuminates all the darkness of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) and delusion (<s>moha</s>). It breaks the four <s>Māras</s> and the deeds of <s>Māra</s>. It destroys the wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) of all <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers). It extinguishes the great blaze of all afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>). It removes the formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) generated by the condition of ignorance. It cuts the six grave diseases (<s>guruvyādhi</s>): greed (<s>lobha</s>), jealousy (<s>mātsarya</s>), breach of morality (<s>śīlabheda</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), laziness (<s>kausīdya</s>), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), and delusion (<s>mūḍhatā</s>). It removes the obstruction of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāvaraṇa</s>), the obstruction of ripening (<s>vipākāvaraṇa</s>), the obstruction of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>), the obstruction of views (<s>dṛṣṭyāvaraṇa</s>), the obstruction of ignorance (<s>avidyāvaraṇa</s>), the obstruction of knowledge (<s>jñānāvaraṇa</s>), and the obstruction of existence (<s>bhavāvaraṇa</s>). Stated briefly: this <s>sūtra</s> extinguishes without remainder all unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>. It nourishes the blazing mass of all wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Sons and daughters of good family, having heard this <s>sūtra</s>, if they delight in it, rejoice in it, and generate a mind of wonder — it should be known that they have worshipped immeasurable <s>Buddhas</s>. Profound roots of merit (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) have been planted. For what reason? Because this <s>sūtra</s> has been practiced by <s>Buddhas</s> in the three times. Indeed, a practitioner of the path (<s>mārgāvacara</s>) who hears this <s>sūtra</s> considers himself blessed, and he obtains the great gain of wholesomeness. Whoever writes and recites this <s>sūtra</s> — it should be known that such a person obtains immeasurable, limitless ripening of the fruit of merit. For what reason? Because this <s>sūtra</s> has limitless support, because it generates immeasurable great vows (<s>mahāpraṇidhāna</s>), because it benefits all beings, because it accomplishes unsurpassed perfect awakening — therefore the ripening of the fruit of merit obtained is also immeasurable. If anyone understands the meaning and practices accordingly, as was spoken by all <s>Buddhas</s> in incalculable <s>kalpas</s> through inexhaustible wisdom — the ripening of the fruit of merit of that person is also inexhaustible. In whatever place a teacher of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmaśāstṛ</s>) teaches this <s>sūtra</s>, it should be known that in that place a <s>stūpa</s> should be erected. Why? Because the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>samyagdharma</s>) has been born there. Wherever this <s>sūtra</s> exists — in whatever land, city, village, monastery (<s>vihāra</s>), or hut — it should be known that there the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body) of the <s>Tathāgata</s> exists. If a person worships [it] with fragrance and flowers, with song, with canopies, with yak-tail fans and parasols, with hymns, with praises, and with salutations — it should be known that such a person greatly increases the <s>Buddha</s>-seed. How much more needless to say about one who grasps and retains this <s>sūtra</s> without remainder! Such a person fulfills the accomplishment of merit and wisdom (<s>puṇyaprajñāniṣpatti</s>), in the future receives a prophecy (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>), and attains the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: (iti bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstre puṇyaparigraho nāma dvādaśo vargaḥ ||)
body.translated_text: (Thus, in the <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s>, the twelfth chapter called 'The Gathering of Merit' (<s>Puṇyaparigraha</s>) [is concluded].)

body.text: pariniṣṭhitaṃ bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstram ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhicittotpādasūtraśāstra</s> is completed.
